elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate an integration harness that instantiates a DUT with the exact module name `i2c_master_bit_ctrl`, no parameters, and the specified port names and directions; drive clk, rst, nReset, ena, clk_cnt, cmd, din, scl_i, and sda_i with legal values.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of `shows`: elaboration succeeds, the instance resolves specifically to `i2c_master_bit_ctrl`, all specified connections bind, and the simulation starts with observable DUT outputs present.
elements.check_method: Use the simulator/compiler elaboration result and hierarchy database to assert successful compilation, exact instance/module-name resolution, zero unconnected required ports, and presence of the expected output and probe signals.

elements.stimulus: Use the identical integration harness, but remove the `i2c_master_bit_ctrl` module from the compiled sources or rename it so that no module with that exact name is available.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case of `shows`: elaboration fails because the required `i2c_master_bit_ctrl` bit-controller instance cannot be resolved; no DUT outputs or simulation hierarchy for that controller are produced.
elements.check_method: Assert a nonzero compile/elaboration result and match the diagnostic or unresolved-instance report for the missing exact module name; reject any result that silently substitutes another module.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=3, release both external bus lines high, and issue cmd=START while idle. Hold cmd stable until command acceptance, then leave the bus released externally.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: scl_oen and sda_oen produce the START sequence: both are released, SDA is driven low while SCL remains released high, then SCL is driven low; the sequence completes with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_oen and sda_oen against a reference model of the enabled prescaler and START FSM phases; verify SDA-low/SCL-high ordering and exactly one terminal cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: Establish a busy bus using a completed START, keep ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, then issue cmd=STOP while idle with the external SCL line able to rise.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: scl_oen and sda_oen produce the STOP sequence: SDA is driven low, SCL is released high, and SDA is then released high while SCL is high; the sequence completes with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model to compare both output-enable waveforms and verify the required STOP phase ordering, completion pulse, and no premature SDA release before SCL is released high.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, clk_cnt=3, and the external bus initially high, issue cmd=WRITE with din=0 while idle; allow the external SCL line to follow the controller without stretching.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: sda_oen drives SDA low for din=0, scl_oen releases SCL for the high phase, then drives SCL low; the command-specific sequence completes with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Compare registered scl_oen and sda_oen after every posedge with the WRITE(din=0) reference waveform; check active-low output-enable polarity, SCL phase ordering, and one-cycle completion acknowledgement.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, clk_cnt=3, and the external bus initially high, issue cmd=WRITE with din=1 while idle; keep SDA externally high during the released high phase so arbitration is not lost.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: sda_oen releases SDA for din=1, scl_oen releases SCL for the high phase, then drives SCL low; the command-specific sequence completes with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_oen and sda_oen cycle-by-cycle with the WRITE(din=1) reference model, explicitly checking that SDA is released rather than driven low and that the sequence reaches cmd_ack without arbitration loss.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, clk_cnt=3, and the external bus initially high, issue cmd=READ while idle. Release SDA externally, drive the returned read bit high during the SCL high window, and allow SCL to rise and fall without stretching.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: sda_oen remains released so the external device can drive SDA, scl_oen releases SCL for the read window, then drives SCL low; the command-specific sequence completes with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use the timed READ reference model to compare both output-enable sequences at each settled posedge, verify SDA remains released throughout the read window, and verify completion after the low phase.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, clk_cnt=3, and the external bus initially high, issue cmd=WRITE with din=1 and wait until the command has entered its timed sequence with SDA released and SCL released. Assert nReset=0 asynchronously between clock edges, then deassert it before the next command.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise case of shows: scl_oen and sda_oen do not complete the command-specific sequence through cmd_ack; reset aborts the sequence and releases both lines, with no completion acknowledgement for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: Check output enables immediately after asynchronous reset assertion and on the following settled clock; verify both are released, the in-progress command does not resume or acknowledge, and compare the observed trace against the reset/abort reference model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, present cmd=START with clk_cnt=0, and keep external SCL and SDA released high. Continue clocking until the command completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for cmd_ack, busy, scl_oen, and sda_oen: the controller generates START by releasing SCL and SDA, then driving SDA low while SCL is high and subsequently driving SCL low; cmd_ack produces exactly one clock pulse at the terminal phase, and busy becomes asserted after the filtered START is detected.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, compare cmd_ack, busy, scl_oen, and sda_oen against a transaction reference model; assert the required output-enable ordering, one-cycle acknowledgment width, and busy assertion after filtered START.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and present cmd=NOP, then exercise SDA and SCL without creating a filtered START or STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for cmd_ack, busy, scl_oen, and sda_oen: no command-complete pulse occurs, busy does not change, and no START/STOP command-specific output-enable sequence is generated; the controller remains in its idle released-line behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor the outputs for the complete observation window and compare with the idle reference model; assert cmd_ack remains low, busy remains unchanged, and neither output enable enters a command sequence.

elements.stimulus: First establish busy with a filtered START, then set ena=1 and issue cmd=STOP with clk_cnt=0. Keep the bus available for SCL release and external high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for STOP behavior: the controller drives SDA low, releases SCL and waits for filtered SCL high, then releases SDA while SCL is high; cmd_ack is a one-clock pulse at completion and busy clears after the filtered STOP is detected.
elements.check_method: Use a phase-aware reference model to compare scl_oen, sda_oen, cmd_ack, and busy on each settled posedge; verify STOP ordering, completion pulse width, and busy deassertion.

elements.stimulus: While idle or during a non-command bus interval, apply SDA transitions that are shorter than the filter interval or occur while filtered SCL is low, and do not issue a STOP command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for busy and STOP output behavior: no filtered STOP is recognized, busy does not clear because of the transient activity, no cmd_ack is generated, and no STOP-specific SDA/SCL release sequence occurs.
elements.check_method: Model the synchronizer and majority filter, then assert that sta_condition and sto_condition remain inactive and that busy, cmd_ack, scl_oen, and sda_oen match the non-command reference behavior.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=WRITE with din=0, then repeat with din=1. Keep SCL externally high whenever released and keep SDA consistent with the transmitted value.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for single-bit WRITE: for din=0, sda_oen drives SDA low; for din=1, sda_oen releases SDA. In both cases the controller releases SCL for the high phase, pulls SCL low, produces one cmd_ack pulse, and leaves al deasserted when the external SDA agrees.
elements.check_method: Run both data values through a cycle-accurate command reference model and compare sda_oen, scl_oen, cmd_ack, and al; verify polarity and phase ordering separately for din=0 and din=1.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, issue cmd=WRITE with din=1. During the released-high SDA arbitration phase, externally hold SDA low while SCL is filtered high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for arbitration-loss detection: al asserts, the active WRITE aborts without cmd_ack, the FSM returns idle, and both scl_oen and sda_oen release their lines. al remains asserted until reset.
elements.check_method: Detect the filtered SDA-low condition during the WRITE released-high phase and compare outputs with the arbitration-loss reference model; assert no acknowledgment and sticky al until reset.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=WRITE with din=0 and externally hold SDA low during the released-high phase; separately issue a WRITE with din=1 while SDA remains high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for arbitration loss: al remains deasserted for din=0 despite SDA being low, and also remains deasserted for din=1 when SDA is high; each valid WRITE completes with exactly one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Run both cases in the reference model with arbitration checking enabled only when din=1; assert completion and absence of al in both cases.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, issue cmd=READ using clk_cnt=1. Release SDA for the read window, have the external device drive SDA low for one run and high for another, and provide a normal filtered SCL rising edge followed by SCL low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for single-bit READ: sda_oen releases SDA, scl_oen releases SCL for the read window, dout captures the filtered SDA value exactly at the filtered SCL rising edge for each run, SCL is then driven low, and cmd_ack pulses once after the low phase.
elements.check_method: Use synchronized-input and filter modeling to identify filtered_scl_rising; compare dout capture timing and value plus scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack against the READ reference model.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=READ, keep filtered SCL low after the controller releases it, and do not provide a filtered SCL rising edge during the observation interval.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for READ capture and completion: dout does not update for a READ bit, cmd_ack is not generated, and the controller holds the released-high timing phase instead of advancing to completion while SCL remains filtered low.
elements.check_method: Assert that no filtered_scl_rising event occurs and compare dout, cmd_ack, scl_oen, and the internal wait behavior with the stalled READ reference model.

elements.stimulus: Issue a supported START, WRITE, or READ command with SCL released by the controller, then externally hold SCL low for multiple enabled clocks before releasing it high; repeat with an external SCL falling edge occurring after release.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for slave stretching and multi-master clock synchronization: the controller pauses timing and FSM progress while filtered SCL is low, does not complete the command during the stretch, and resumes phase timing only after filtered SCL becomes high. A filtered external SCL falling edge while released causes timing synchronization/reload before progress resumes.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_oen, cmd_ack, and phase transitions with a divider/stretching/synchronization reference model; assert no phase advancement during slave_wait and verify completion only after the synchronized high period.

elements.stimulus: Issue the same supported command with SCL remaining high whenever released and with no external falling edge or clock stretch; use clk_cnt values 0, 1, and a larger value.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for stretch/synchronization: no slave-wait extension or multi-master resynchronization occurs, the FSM advances on normal clk_en ticks, and each command completes with the expected phase order and one cmd_ack pulse at a latency determined only by the prescaler and filtering.
elements.check_method: Compare phase timing and completion against a reference model for each clk_cnt value; assert no unexpected stall, synchronization reload, or missing acknowledgment.

elements.stimulus: After reset, apply raw SDA and SCL pulses shorter than the filter sampling interval, then apply stable SDA falling and rising transitions while SCL is stably high. Exercise the sequence with ena=1.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for synchronized and glitch-filtered inputs: short raw glitches do not cause busy changes, arbitration loss, command acknowledgment, or command-specific output-enable activity; stable filtered transitions are recognized as START and STOP, causing busy to assert and then clear.
elements.check_method: Model two-stage synchronization, filter history, majority filtering, and delayed values; correlate sta_condition/sto_condition with busy and verify only stable filtered transitions affect observable outputs.

elements.stimulus: Keep SDA and SCL transitions either unsynchronized, shorter than the filter interval, or at filtered SCL low, and issue no supported command requiring a bus operation.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for synchronized/filter behavior: no filtered START or STOP is detected, busy remains unchanged, al remains deasserted, dout does not capture a READ bit, cmd_ack remains low, and scl_oen/sda_oen remain in idle behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the input synchronization/filter reference model to prove that no qualifying filtered edge or condition occurred, then assert all observable outputs remain at their non-operation values.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous reset, then set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and drive both external bus lines high. Issue a START command and sample the output interface during the START phase in which SDA is pulled low while SCL remains released.
elements.expected_response: This is the 'shows' side for the drive case: scl_o and sda_o remain 0, scl_oen is 1 so SCL is released, and sda_oen is 0 so SDA is actively driven low. The resulting open-drain bus levels are SCL high and SDA low.
elements.check_method: After every relevant posedge, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0; during the START drive phase assert scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==0, and compare the resolved bus levels against the external-drive model.

elements.stimulus: Complete a START command on a released-high bus, then issue a STOP command with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Sample the output interface first while SDA is driven low and then during the STOP phases after SCL and SDA are released; optionally pull either external line low while its DUT output enable is released.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting 'shows' side for release versus drive: scl_o and sda_o remain 0 throughout; sda_oen is 0 while STOP initially drives SDA low, then scl_oen becomes 1 to release SCL and sda_oen becomes 1 to release SDA while SCL is high. If an external participant pulls a released line low, the DUT does not drive it high.
elements.check_method: Use temporal assertions on the registered enables: STOP drive phase has sda_oen==0, SCL-release phase has scl_oen==1, and final SDA-release phase has sda_oen==1. Continuously assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0, and verify resolved line levels follow wired-AND open-drain resolution when external low drives are applied.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high external bus, and issue cmd=START with clk_cnt=0. Observe the START sequence through completion, including the phase where SDA is pulled low while SCL remains released high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for the active-low controls: scl_o and sda_o are always 0; during the START condition phase scl_oen=1, so SCL is released, and sda_oen=0, so SDA is driven low. The corresponding bus lines are therefore SCL high and SDA low, and the START command eventually produces one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge from reset release through command completion, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0. During the START SDA-low/SCL-high phase, compare scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==0 and independently resolve the open-drain bus value from the enable and external pull-up model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high external bus, and issue cmd=READ with clk_cnt=0. Keep the external SDA high and allow the controller to enter and complete the read high phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting release case for the active-low controls: scl_o and sda_o are always 0; during the READ window scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, so both SCL and SDA are released and may remain high through the external pull-ups. The READ command completes with one cmd_ack pulse and no arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge from reset release through command completion, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0. During the READ released-line window, compare scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==1 and resolve both bus levels as high when no external participant drives low; verify the command completion pulse and al==0.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, then deassert it with ena high and scl_i/sda_i externally released high. After reset settles, sample scl_oen=1 and resolve the SCL line with no external low driver.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in shows: scl_oen=1 releases SCL, so the resolved SCL line is high due to the external pull-up; it must not be driven low by the DUT.
elements.check_method: After asynchronous reset, compare scl_oen to the resolved wired-open-drain SCL model: with no external low driver, require scl_oen=1 and SCL high. Also require scl_o=0.

elements.stimulus: Deassert reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the bus externally released high, and issue a START command. Follow the command sequence until the START phase pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in shows for the low state: when scl_oen=0 during the START sequence, the corresponding SCL line is pulled low, regardless of the external pull-up.
elements.check_method: At each registered output update after a posedge, detect the START phase with scl_oen=0 and compare the resolved SCL line to low. Require scl_o=0 and no external participant driving SCL low.

elements.stimulus: Deassert reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the bus externally released high, and issue a START command. During the START sequence, observe the phase in which SDA is pulled low while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in shows for SDA low: when sda_oen=0, the corresponding SDA line is pulled low even though the external pull-up is present.
elements.check_method: During the registered START output phase, require sda_oen=0 and resolve SDA with no external low driver; compare the resolved SDA line to low. Require sda_o=0.

elements.stimulus: Deassert reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep SCL and SDA externally released high, and issue a READ command. Observe the READ data window after the command is accepted.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting case in shows: during READ, sda_oen=1 releases SDA, so with no external low driver the SDA line is high from the external pull-up; it must not be driven low by the DUT.
elements.check_method: During the registered READ data-window phase, require sda_oen=1 and compare the resolved SDA line to high with the external device not driving low. Also require sda_o=0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive nReset=1, rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Issue cmd=4'b0001 (START) for an enabled clock tick, then continue providing enabled clocks with the bus released high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen and sda_oen perform the commanded timed bit-level START sequence: both lines are initially released, SDA is pulled low while SCL remains released high, then SCL is pulled low, followed by exactly one cmd_ack pulse. This demonstrates the module's Bit Command Controller behavior through its observable output-enable ports.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_oen and sda_oen against a reference START-sequence model and verify the sequence reaches exactly one cmd_ack pulse without reset or arbitration loss.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive nReset=1, rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. While idle, issue unsupported cmd=4'b0011 for multiple enabled clock ticks, then return cmd to 4'b0000.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise case: scl_oen and sda_oen do not produce any commanded START, STOP, READ, or WRITE bit-level sequence; both remain released high, and no cmd_ack pulse occurs. This is the observable no-corresponding-command window contrasted with the Bit Command Controller behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack over the complete stimulus window; assert that no output-enable transition matching a command sequence occurs and that cmd_ack remains low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=START (4'b0001), and provide an externally released-high SCL and SDA bus. Hold cmd until the controller accepts it, then observe the complete START command sequence.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0007: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0 throughout. scl_oen initially releases SCL, then changes to drive SCL low after SDA has been driven low; sda_oen initially releases SDA, then changes to drive SDA low while SCL is released high. The observed enable transitions form the commanded START line behavior, followed by command completion.
elements.check_method: At every enabled command phase, compare scl_o and sda_o against constant 0 and compare the sampled scl_oen/sda_oen waveform against a reference START-sequence model, allowing registered one-clock output latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset and while idle, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and apply cmd=NOP (4'b0000), then each unsupported encoding 4'b0011, 4'b0101, and 4'b1111 for multiple enabled clocks while the external SCL and SDA bus remain released high.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case for REQ-0007: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0, while scl_oen and sda_oen remain in their released-high idle values and do not produce any command-driven SCL or SDA phase transitions; no command-complete pulse is generated.
elements.check_method: Monitor the output-enable waveform over all applied unsupported-command intervals and assert that it stays at the reset/idle released values, that scl_o and sda_o are always 0, and that cmd_ack remains low; compare against the idle/no-command reference model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, cmd=START, and keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 so the bus is released high. Drive clocks until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: from command acceptance through cmd_ack, scl_oen and sda_oen show the START bit-level sequence: both lines are released initially, SDA is driven low while SCL remains released high, then SCL is driven low, followed by exactly one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: A scoreboard samples registered scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack after each posedge and compares the observed ordered phases with the START reference sequence; require no missing, extra, or reordered phase.

elements.stimulus: After establishing a busy bus with a completed START, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, cmd=STOP, and keep the externally observed SCL high when released. Drive clocks until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: from STOP acceptance through cmd_ack, scl_oen and sda_oen show the STOP bit-level sequence: SDA is driven low, SCL is released high, then SDA is released high while SCL is high, followed by exactly one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Compare the registered output-enable trace against a STOP phase scoreboard, checking the required SDA-low, SCL-release, and SDA-release ordering and the terminal ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, cmd=READ, and drive the external bus with a valid read bit: release SCL when requested and return sda_i=1 during the read window. Drive clocks until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: from READ acceptance through cmd_ack, sda_oen remains released for the slave-driven data bit, scl_oen releases SCL for the read window, then drives SCL low for completion, followed by exactly one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a READ reference scoreboard to check the ordered sda_oen release, scl_oen release/high phase, scl_oen low phase, and terminal cmd_ack; also confirm the returned bit is captured without changing the required output-enable sequence.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, cmd=WRITE and din=0, with the external bus initially high and able to rise when SCL is released. Drive clocks until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: from WRITE acceptance through cmd_ack, sda_oen drives SDA low for din=0, scl_oen releases SCL for the write high phase, then drives SCL low, followed by exactly one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Compare registered scl_oen and sda_oen samples to the WRITE(din=0) reference sequence and verify the sequence terminates with one cmd_ack and no arbitration-loss abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset, while idle and ena=1, apply cmd=NOP=0000 for multiple clk_en opportunities, then apply unsupported cmd values 0011, 0101, 0111, 1001, 1010, 1011, 1100, 1101, 1110, and 1111, one at a time, without issuing a supported command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: scl_oen and sda_oen do not show any corresponding START, STOP, READ, or WRITE command-specific bit-level sequence; they remain in the idle released-line behavior, and no cmd_ack is generated.
elements.check_method: For each no-op or unsupported command, assert that the output-enable trace contains no command-phase transition before the next command and that cmd_ack remains low; compare against the idle reference model.

elements.stimulus: Instantiate i2c_master_bit_ctrl from a downstream testbench, connect clk, rst, nReset, ena as 1-bit inputs, connect clk_cnt as a 16-bit input, and elaborate the design with clk_cnt driven at 16'h0000 and 16'hFFFF.
elements.expected_response: REQ-0009 holds: elaboration succeeds and the instance accepts clk, rst, nReset, and ena as input ports and accepts the full 16-bit clk_cnt input without width or direction diagnostics.
elements.check_method: Run the HDL compiler/elaborator with warnings promoted to errors for port direction and width mismatches; require successful elaboration and inspect the resolved port widths and directions in the elaboration report.

elements.stimulus: Run the same downstream instantiation against a deliberately nonconforming DUT interface variant in which one of clk, rst, nReset, or ena is not an input, or clk_cnt is declared with a width other than 16 bits.
elements.expected_response: REQ-0009 does not hold: downstream elaboration must reject the instance or report a port direction/width mismatch for the altered interface; it must not silently accept the nonconforming declaration as the specified interface.
elements.check_method: Compile and elaborate the negative-control variant with port mismatches treated as errors, then compare diagnostics and resolved interface metadata against the required five input ports and 16-bit clk_cnt declaration.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate the DUT using its declared interface, with cmd connected as a 4-bit input and cmd_ack, busy, and al connected as output signals.
elements.expected_response: The module interface declares cmd as an input port and declares cmd_ack, busy, and al as output ports. This is the holding case of the requirement's shows condition.
elements.check_method: Use a Verilog parser or elaboration reflection to inspect the module port list, directions, and widths; fail unless cmd is input [3:0] and cmd_ack, busy, and al are outputs.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate a negative interface variant in which cmd_ack, busy, or al is omitted or changed from an output declaration to an input or otherwise non-output declaration.
elements.expected_response: The interface checker reports a structural violation because the affected port is absent or is not declared as an output. This is the contrasting case of the requirement's shows condition.
elements.check_method: Run compile-time port-direction and presence assertions against the mutated variant and require a diagnostic or assertion failure for each omitted or incorrectly directed port.

elements.stimulus: Inspect the elaborated module interface declaration for i2c_master_bit_ctrl, including the boundary ports din and dout.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: dout is present as a one-bit output and din is present as a one-bit input.
elements.check_method: Parse the elaborated HDL port list or compile-time interface metadata and assert direction=input for din, direction=output for dout, and width=1 for both.

elements.stimulus: Run interface validation against variants in which dout is absent, dout is not an output, dout is wider than one bit, din is absent, din is not an input, or din is wider than one bit.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the interface is reported as nonconforming because dout is absent or is not a one-bit output, or din is absent or is not a one-bit input.
elements.check_method: Compile or run the interface linter for each malformed variant and require a diagnostic or validation failure identifying the missing, misdirected, or incorrectly sized port.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate the DUT with ports scl_i and sda_i connected as input nets and scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, and sda_oen connected as output nets; inspect the elaborated module port directions and widths.
elements.expected_response: At module interface elaboration, scl_i and sda_i are input ports, and scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, and sda_oen are output ports. This is the required side of the port-direction distinction.
elements.check_method: Use simulator/VPI or elaboration metadata to compare each port's declared direction and width against the interface contract; require successful elaboration with all six named connections.

elements.stimulus: Run a negative-control elaboration using an interface-mutated DUT in which each of scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, and sda_oen is absent or declared as an input instead of an output, while the testbench still requires the specified output connections.
elements.expected_response: Elaboration or interface-contract checking rejects the mutated interface, identifying that scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, and sda_oen are not declared as output ports. This is the contrasting, non-holding side of the port-direction distinction.
elements.check_method: Expect a nonzero compile/elaboration result or a structural-interface assertion failure, and match diagnostics or introspection results to each required output port; do not accept a run that treats the mutated ports as valid outputs.

elements.stimulus: Inspect the module specification and elaborated interface at the input-port declaration section.
elements.expected_response: The specification contains an input-port declaration section, and the module interface is accepted without treating that section as executable runtime behavior.
elements.check_method: Static specification review plus parser/elaboration check confirming the input-port declarations are present and syntactically valid.

elements.stimulus: Run clk with a stable period, keep nReset deasserted and ena high, issue a supported START command while the bus is released high, and continue clocking until the command reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Shows side of REQ-0014: cmd_ack asserts on exactly one rising edge of clk at START completion, remains asserted for that one clock cycle, deasserts on the next rising edge, and is stable between rising edges.
elements.check_method: Use a clock-aware waveform monitor sampling immediately after each posedge and at intervening non-rising times; compare cmd_ack against a reference model keyed to the terminal START phase and require exactly one rising-edge-aligned pulse.

elements.stimulus: Run clk with a stable period, issue a supported READ command with ena high, and observe cmd_ack continuously across both rising and falling edges during command completion, including at least two non-rising sampling points between adjacent rising edges.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise side is checked as a forbidden outcome: cmd_ack must not change at a falling or any other non-rising edge, must not pulse more than once between consecutive rising edges, and must remain stable between rising edges; only the single rising-edge-aligned completion pulse is permitted.
elements.check_method: Use an edge-sensitive assertion and waveform monitor that records every cmd_ack transition with the clk level and edge type; fail if any transition occurs when clk is not rising or if more than one transition interval is observed between consecutive rising edges.

elements.stimulus: Hold ena high, set clk_cnt to 0, keep the bus released and valid, issue a supported START command before a rising edge, and continue clocking until the command reaches its terminal phase. Repeat for command completion so both cmd_ack assertion and deassertion are observed.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack changes only immediately after a rising edge that processes the command terminal phase. It remains asserted for exactly one clock interval and deasserts only on a subsequent rising edge; it is stable throughout each interval between rising edges.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk, sample cmd_ack after sequential updates settle and compare it with samples taken continuously or at both half-cycle boundaries until the next posedge. Assert that every cmd_ack transition is associated with the immediately preceding posedge and that the pulse width is one clock period.

elements.stimulus: While idle, change cmd between rising edges, including changing from NOP to START and back to NOP at a falling edge, with ena high and clk_cnt set to 0. Also perform the same mid-cycle input changes while an accepted command is active, without changing clk or applying reset.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting-case check: cmd_ack must not assert, deassert, or otherwise change in response to a mid-cycle cmd change or at a falling edge. If any cmd_ack transition is observed between rising edges, that is a failure of the required synchronous-update behavior; cmd_ack may change only on a rising-edge update.
elements.check_method: Use a clocking-block or event-based monitor to record cmd_ack immediately before and after every falling edge and throughout each interval between posedges. Correlate every detected transition with a posedge clk; flag any transition lacking such a rising-edge cause.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt=0 and ena=1. Initialize with nReset low then high. With scl_i and sda_i released high, issue cmd=START and allow the filtered START condition to be detected so busy is high. Assert rst=1 through a rising edge of clk, then deassert rst.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the rising edge while rst is high, busy is reset low, demonstrating synchronous reset of the bus-status state; the command FSM, counters, and filtered-input state also return to their reset behavior.
elements.check_method: At the sampled posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, compare busy against a reference reset model and require busy==0. Check that reset-state probes idle, clk_en/counters, and filtered histories match the initialized model.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt=0 and ena=1. Initialize with nReset low then high. With scl_i and sda_i released high, issue cmd=START and allow busy to become high from the filtered START condition. Keep rst=0 at a rising edge of clk and do not issue STOP or any other command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because rst is not asserted high at the rising edge, busy is not synchronously reset by REQ-0016 and remains high under the ordinary bus-status behavior.
elements.check_method: Sample busy after the rising edge and compare it with the no-reset reference model; require busy to remain high in the absence of a filtered STOP or another status-changing event.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt=0 and ena=1. Initialize with nReset low then high. Issue cmd=WRITE with din=1, allow the WRITE sequence to release SDA during its stable high phase, and externally hold sda_i low so arbitration loss is detected and al becomes high. Assert rst=1 through a rising edge of clk, then deassert rst.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the rising edge while rst is high, al is reset low, demonstrating synchronous reset of the arbitration-status state; the command FSM and associated internal state are reset as well.
elements.check_method: After the reset posedge settles, compare al and the FSM state with a reference reset model and require al==0 and idle==1. Confirm no stale command completion pulse is produced by the reset.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt=0 and ena=1. Initialize with nReset low then high. Issue cmd=WRITE with din=1, externally hold sda_i low during the released SDA high phase until al becomes high. Keep rst=0 at a rising edge of clk and do not assert either reset input.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because rst is not asserted high at the rising edge, al is not synchronously reset by REQ-0016 and retains its prior arbitration-lost status.
elements.check_method: Sample al after the rising edge and compare it with the no-reset reference model; require al to remain high and sticky while no reset is asserted.

elements.stimulus: Start from an active controller state with nReset high, then assert nReset low between two rising edges of clk and hold it low; sample scl_oen immediately before the next clock edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: scl_oen becomes 1 immediately when nReset is asserted low, without waiting for a clk edge, consistent with asynchronous reset initialization.
elements.check_method: At the nReset falling edge, use an asynchronous monitor or sampled-value check before the next clk posedge to require scl_oen == 1; also check that sda_oen is released and registered status outputs are cleared.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset high, issue a valid START command with ena high and clk_cnt selected to allow progress, and wait until the START sequence has pulled SCL low; do not assert either reset input during this interval.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of shows: with nReset high during normal active operation, scl_oen is controlled by the current FSM phase and may remain 0 during the active SCL-low phase rather than immediately becoming 1.
elements.check_method: Use the start_sequence and output-enable phase probes to identify the SCL-low phase, then compare the registered scl_oen value after the corresponding posedge and require scl_oen == 0 while nReset remains high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold the bus released-high, set clk_cnt to 0, drive a supported START command, and hold ena high until the command completes.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-high side of the observation: the command sequence progresses from idle to completion and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare cmd_ack and the command-sequence progress against a reference model; require exactly one cmd_ack pulse and no additional pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold the bus released-high, drive a supported START command while the controller is idle, and hold ena low throughout the command-completion observation window.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-low side of the observation: command acceptance and progression are disabled, so cmd_ack does not pulse during the observation window.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack and command-sequence probes on every settled posedge while ena is low; require no cmd_ack pulse and no FSM progression from idle, comparing against the disabled-enable reference-model behavior.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a nonzero value, issue a valid START command, and wait until the START sequence is active but before its terminal phase. Then drive ena=0 and hold it low for several clock cycles while keeping the bus released high.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-low holding case: normal timing is gated off, the active command does not advance to completion, and cmd_ack does not pulse during the ena-low interval. busy does not change due to command completion during that interval.
elements.check_method: At every posedge while ena=0, compare cmd_ack and the command-phase progress against a reference model with timing and FSM advancement disabled; assert cmd_ack remains low and that no terminal-phase transition occurs until ena is reasserted.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset, clk_cnt, START command, and active-command setup, but keep ena=1 throughout the sequence and keep the bus released high.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-high contrasting case: normal timing and filter operation proceed, the START sequence reaches its terminal phase, and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock. This is the ordinary behavior contrasted with the ena-low case.
elements.check_method: Use a divider/FSM reference model to predict enabled timing ticks and terminal-phase completion; compare the predicted completion cycle with the observed one-cycle cmd_ack pulse and verify it occurs without an ena-low interval.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT and establish filtered SCL high and filtered SDA high with the bus released. Drive ena=0, then apply a stable external SDA high-to-low transition while holding SCL high and keep the new SDA level stable for longer than the normal filter interval.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-low filtering case: filter progression is gated off, the stable raw transition does not produce a filtered START detection, and busy does not set because the disabled filter does not propagate the transition.
elements.check_method: Monitor sscl, ssda, fsda, filter_cnt, and busy on each posedge; compare them with a reference model in which filter samples do not shift while ena=0, and assert that no filtered SDA falling edge or busy assertion occurs.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset and bus setup, but keep ena=1 while applying the stable SDA high-to-low transition with SCL high; hold the levels long enough for synchronization and filtering to complete.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-high contrasting case: the transition propagates through filtering, produces a filtered START detection, and busy sets. This ordinary behavior contrasts with the absence of detection and busy assertion when ena is low.
elements.check_method: Model the synchronizer, filter sampling, majority result, and START edge detector; compare ssda and sta_condition against the model and verify busy asserts on the registered cycle following the filtered START processing.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to 8, keep nReset high and rst low, issue a START command with ena high, and after the START sequence is active assert ena low for at least 6 rising edges of clk. Monitor filter_cnt and clk_en on every rising edge while ena is low; then release ena high.
elements.expected_response: While ena is low, filter_cnt is held at its reset value, clk_en remains low on every clock, and no command-phase timing progresses. After ena returns high, timing restarts from the reloaded divider/filter state rather than continuing from the pre-pause phase.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the divider and filter counter. At each posedge compare filter_cnt with the model's reset value and assert clk_en == 0 while ena == 0; after re-enabling, compare the first subsequent clk_en and filter-counter evolution against a freshly reloaded model.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to 8, reset the DUT, issue the same START command with ena continuously high, and observe at least 6 rising edges of clk while the START sequence is active.
elements.expected_response: With ena high, the divider and input filter counter follow their normal progression: filter_cnt is not continuously held at its reset value and clk_en asserts at the model-predicted timing ticks, allowing normal bit-timing progression. This is the contrasting non-holding case for ena low.
elements.check_method: Run the same cycle-accurate divider/filter reference model with ena high and compare filter_cnt and clk_en after every posedge; require at least one model-predicted clk_en tick and corresponding active timing progression during the observation window.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it, keep rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0003, hold the bus released high, then issue a START command and continue clocking for multiple divider periods.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the supplied clk_cnt value is loaded into the timing divider; cnt decreases while enabled, clk_en asserts when the divider expires, reloads, and repeats at the modeled interval. The START FSM advances only on those clk_en ticks, producing the START output phases rather than advancing every system clock.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate divider reference model seeded at reset and command acceptance. At every posedge compare the observed clk_en probe with the model, verify no early or missing tick, and verify START-state/output-enable transitions occur only on cycles with clk_en.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it, keep rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000, hold the bus released high, then issue a START command while clocking for several enabled cycles.
elements.expected_response: Holding case at the minimum value: clk_cnt=0 is loaded without creating a stuck divider, clk_en asserts on every enabled clock according to the defined zero-prescaler behavior, and the START FSM can advance on each such tick.
elements.check_method: Compare clk_en on each posedge against a reference model that treats a zero reload value as an every-enabled-clock tick; check that the START sequence progresses on successive clk_en cycles and that no multi-cycle interval without clk_en occurs while ena remains high.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt=16'h0003, assert nReset low and release it, keep rst low, drive ena=0, issue a START command, and clock for several cycles; then set ena=1 and continue clocking.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case where the requirement is not active: while ena=0, the divider is reloaded/reset for enable, clk_en remains deasserted, the START command is not accepted, and the FSM does not advance. After ena returns high, divider timing resumes from the defined reload behavior and clk_en is generated according to clk_cnt, allowing command acceptance only on a subsequent tick.
elements.check_method: Monitor clk_en, idle/fsm_active probes, and command outputs each posedge. Assert that no clk_en or FSM transition occurs during the disabled interval, then compare post-enable ticks and first command acceptance against the divider reference model.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, keep rst low and ena high, set clk_cnt=16'd8, hold scl_i and sda_i high, and run consecutive rising edges of clk long enough to observe multiple filter_cnt expiries and fSCL/fSDA sampling updates.
elements.expected_response: Requirement-holds case: filter_cnt derives the SDA/SCL filter sampling interval from clk_cnt. With clk_cnt=8, the reference interval is floor(8/4)=2 enabled clocks; filter_cnt expires and shifts synchronized samples into the filter histories at that cadence, with no filter sampling update on the intervening enabled clock.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the enabled-clock divider and floor(clk_cnt/4) filter interval. At each posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, compare filter_cnt expiry and fscl/fsda update events against the predicted two-clock cadence; record a bin for the nominal derived interval.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, keep rst low and ena high, set clk_cnt=16'd0, hold scl_i and sda_i high, and run consecutive rising edges of clk for several enabled cycles.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting boundary case: clk_cnt=0 produces the safe minimum filter interval rather than a stuck or disabled filter. filter_cnt expires or permits a filter sampling update on every enabled clock, so fscl and fsda are sampled each enabled cycle; this is the zero-value behavior of the clk_cnt-derived interval.
elements.check_method: Compare filter_cnt and fscl/fsda update events with the reference model that clamps the zero derived interval to one enabled-clock sampling period. Check that no enabled cycle is skipped and that filter_cnt does not remain stuck.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, then drive cmd=4'b0001 (START) from the byte-controller interface for at least one enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed behavior: the 4-bit cmd value is decoded as the supported START command, the START sequence completes, and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock cycle at command completion; no additional cmd_ack pulse occurs.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after reset release, monitor cmd_ack and correlate it with the START command sequence. Assert exactly one high cycle after the sequence completes, followed by low, using a cycle-accurate scoreboard.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, then drive cmd=4'b0011 (an unsupported encoding) for several enabled clock ticks; also repeat with cmd=4'b0000 (NOP).
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case of the observed behavior: each idle or unsupported 4-bit cmd encoding leaves the command controller without a command sequence and cmd_ack remains low for the entire observation window; no acknowledgement pulse is generated.
elements.check_method: Sample cmd_ack and command-related output enables after each posedge for both encodings. Assert cmd_ack is never high and verify no START, STOP, READ, or WRITE output sequence begins.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the bus released high, drive cmd=4'b0001 (I2C_CMD_START), and hold the command until an enabled clock tick accepts it.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: while the FSM is idle and cmd is the supported START encoding, it decodes START and sda_oen transitions from 1 to 0 during the START phase while SCL remains released high.
elements.check_method: After reset deassertion, use a clocked monitor at each posedge after nonblocking updates settle. Confirm idle reset outputs, then require that acceptance of cmd=0001 is followed by start_sequence and an sda_oen 1-to-0 transition before the START command completes.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the bus released high, and while the FSM is idle drive cmd=4'b0000 (NOP); repeat with an unsupported encoding such as cmd=4'b0011, holding each command across an enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: for an idle command that is not START, cmd is not decoded as I2C_CMD_START; sda_oen does not transition from 1 to 0 into the START-phase low state during the scoped acceptance window, and no START output sequence is entered.
elements.check_method: Monitor sda_oen and start_sequence after each enabled acceptance tick. Compare against the START case and assert that sda_oen remains released and start_sequence never becomes active for NOP or unsupported cmd values; also confirm cmd_ack remains low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1 and the FSM idle, drive cmd=4'b0010 (I2C_CMD_STOP), and provide a released-high bus so the STOP sequence can execute. Hold cmd=0010 until the command is accepted on a clk_en tick, then continue observing through the STOP-condition window.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock cycle after the STOP sequence completes, demonstrating that I2C_CMD_STOP is recognized and supported; no additional cmd_ack pulse is produced for that command.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model to identify the clk_en acceptance and STOP terminal phase; assert that cmd_ack is high on exactly one settled post-posedge sample and low on the immediately preceding and following cycles.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1 and the FSM idle, drive unsupported cmd=4'b0011, and hold it for at least the duration needed for a clk_en tick and a complete STOP-command observation window; keep the bus released high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case of shows: cmd_ack does not pulse, demonstrating that the command field did not contain the supported I2C_CMD_STOP command and that the STOP-command completion indication is absent.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack for the entire modeled command-observation window and assert it remains low; compare against the same one-cycle-pulse check used for cmd=0010 to distinguish unsupported-command behavior from STOP recognition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt to 0, hold scl_i and sda_i high with no external arbitration interference, set din to 0, and present cmd=4'b0100 (I2C_CMD_WRITE) while the controller is idle; continue clocking until command completion.
elements.expected_response: The presented I2C_CMD_WRITE command is the supported case: the controller executes the WRITE sequence and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock at completion.
elements.check_method: A scoreboard detects acceptance of cmd=4'b0100 and compares the observed cmd_ack waveform against a reference WRITE model, requiring one and only one high cycle after the terminal WRITE phase and no additional pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt to 0, hold scl_i and sda_i high, and while the controller is idle present unsupported cmd=4'b0011 for multiple enabled clocks, with no valid WRITE command applied.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting unsupported/not-completed case: cmd_ack remains low and no WRITE completion pulse occurs.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack for the entire observation window and compare with the reference idle/no-op model; assert that cmd_ack never rises and that no command-completion event is recorded.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=0, and while the FSM is idle drive cmd successively with NOP=0000 and each unsupported encoding 0011, 0101, 0110, 0111, 1001, 1010, 1011, 1100, 1101, 1110, and 1111; hold each value through an enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: For every idle or unsupported cmd value, the command FSM remains idle, no command sequence starts, and cmd_ack remains low. This is the 'when this requirement holds' side of the port difference.
elements.check_method: At each enabled clock tick, compare the idle probe against 1 and verify it remains asserted; also check read_sequence and fsm_active remain deasserted and cmd_ack has no pulse.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=0, drive cmd=I2C_CMD_READ=1000 while the FSM is idle, and hold it through an enabled clock tick with SDA and SCL released high.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled tick, the READ command is decoded and the FSM leaves idle to begin the READ operation; read_sequence and fsm_active assert, and idle deasserts. This is the contrasting 'when this requirement does not hold' side of the port difference.
elements.check_method: Sample the idle, read_sequence, and fsm_active probes after the enabled posedge and verify idle transitions from 1 to 0 while read_sequence or fsm_active becomes 1; verify the transition is caused by cmd=1000 and not by reset.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=0, and issue cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) while the external SDA and SCL lines are released high. Allow the enabled WRITE sequence to reach its data phase and continue until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data phase, while write_sequence is active and the controller transmits din=0, sda_oen is 0, causing the open-drain DUT to drive SDA low. This is the din=0 side of the requirement's sda_oen behavior.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, identify the data phase using the write_sequence probe and compare registered sda_oen against din; require sda_oen==0 for din==0, no arbitration loss, and eventual cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=1, and issue cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) while an external participant leaves SDA and SCL released high. Allow the enabled WRITE sequence to reach its data phase and continue until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data phase, while write_sequence is active and the controller transmits din=1, sda_oen is 1, releasing SDA so the line remains high. This is the din=1 side of the requirement's sda_oen behavior.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, identify the data phase using the write_sequence probe and compare registered sda_oen against din; require sda_oen==1 for din==1, no arbitration loss, and eventual cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=WRITE, din=0, clk_cnt=0, and keep the externally observed SDA/SCL bus high. Apply the WRITE command through a rising edge that accepts it, then keep din=0 until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-drive phase after command acceptance and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 0, selecting the active-low open-drain driver so SDA is driven low. This is the din=0 side of the specified behavior.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge during the WRITE data-drive phase, compare sda_oen with the reference model expectation sda_oen = 0 for din=0; require the value before the terminal cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=WRITE, din=1, clk_cnt=0, and keep the externally observed SDA/SCL bus high. Apply the WRITE command through a rising edge that accepts it, then keep din=1 until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-drive phase after command acceptance and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 1, releasing SDA so the high bus level is not driven low. This is the din=1 side of the specified behavior and contrasts with the din=0 case.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge during the WRITE data-drive phase, compare sda_oen with the reference model expectation sda_oen = 1 for din=1; require the value before the terminal cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a START command with cmd=0001 while the bus is released high. When the DUT releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1), externally drive scl_i low and hold it low long enough for the synchronized and filtered SCL input to become low.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in REQ-0030's shows text: scl_oen remains 1 and the SCL-high phase is held while the externally driven SCL input remains low; the command phase does not advance until filtered SCL becomes high.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, monitor scl_oen, sscl, slave_wait, and clk_en. Confirm that once scl_oen=1 and sscl=0, scl_oen stays 1, slave_wait is asserted, and no high-phase FSM progression or completion occurs while scl_i remains low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a START command with cmd=0001 while the bus is released high. Keep scl_i externally high after the DUT releases SCL, with no external clock stretching or synchronization event.
elements.expected_response: This is the otherwise case in REQ-0030's shows text: with externally driven SCL high and no stretching or synchronization condition, the timing phase advances and scl_oen eventually returns to 0.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, monitor scl_oen, sscl, clk_en, and the START-sequence probe. Confirm that the filtered SCL becomes high, clk_en permits progression, and scl_oen transitions from 1 back to 0 within the reference-model-predicted phase timing.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a nonzero value. Issue a READ command with the bus initially idle and externally hold scl_i low while the controller reaches the phase that releases SCL; then drive scl_i high and provide a stable SDA value for the read bit.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen remains released during the SCL-high phase while the synchronized and filtered SCL remains low; the READ sequence does not advance to completion and cmd_ack does not pulse. After scl_i is high long enough for synchronization and filtering, the sequence resumes and cmd_ack pulses after the remaining phases.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage SCL synchronizer, filter sampling, majority result, slave_wait, and FSM timing. Assert that scl_oen stays high and cmd_ack stays low during filtered-SCL-low stretching, then compare the modeled completion pulse with the observed cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the enabled READ command with scl_i held high throughout the released-SCL phase and provide stable SDA data before the filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrast case: because synchronized and filtered SCL is high, scl_oen advances through the normal SCL phases without a clock-stretch hold, and cmd_ack pulses at the normal modeled completion point rather than being delayed by slave_wait.
elements.check_method: Run the same reference model with filtered SCL continuously high and compare scl_oen phase transitions and cmd_ack timing against the stretched case; verify no unexpected slave_wait interval is observed.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and issue a WRITE or READ command that releases SCL. After the controller has released SCL and filtered SCL is high, externally pull scl_i low and hold it long enough to pass synchronization and filtering, then release scl_i high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the synchronized and filtered SCL falling edge is recognized as clock synchronization; timing is reloaded, the released-SCL phase is extended, and command completion is delayed until the synchronized and filtered SCL returns high. cmd_ack is not emitted during the synchronization hold.
elements.check_method: Compare cscl, sscl, filtered_scl_falling, scl_sync, cnt_zero, and clk_en with the reference model. Verify the counter reload and delayed scl_oen/cmd_ack progression after the filtered falling edge.

elements.stimulus: Run the same enabled WRITE or READ command with scl_i held high during the entire released-SCL phase and without an external SCL falling edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrast case: no synchronized and filtered SCL falling edge is present, so scl_sync is not asserted, the timing counter is not reloaded for clock synchronization, and cmd_ack occurs at the normal modeled command-completion time.
elements.check_method: Use assertions on cscl, sscl, filtered_scl_falling, scl_sync, cnt_zero, and cmd_ack, and compare the observed timing against a reference run with no external SCL transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the bus filtered high, issue a START command with ena=1, and allow the controller to pull SDA low while filtered scl_i remains high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the filtered SCL-high window qualifies the filtered SDA high-to-low transition as START; busy rises after the registered detection, and the START sequence proceeds to cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Drive the bus through the synchronizer/filter reference model and compare sscl, ssda, dsda, sta_condition, busy, and cmd_ack. Require busy to rise only when the filtered START predicate is true.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and the controller idle, first establish filtered SCL low, then drive SDA from high to low while holding scl_i low; keep the raw transition shorter than the filter interval in a second trial.
elements.expected_response: Contrast case: an SDA transition while synchronized and filtered SCL is low, or a raw glitch rejected by the SCL/SDA filter, is not a qualified START; busy does not rise and no START-related command response occurs.
elements.check_method: Compare sta_condition and busy against the majority-filter reference model. Assert that busy remains unchanged for both the filtered-SCL-low transition and the sub-filter-interval glitch.

elements.stimulus: Create a busy transaction, issue STOP with ena=1, and allow the controller to release SCL high before releasing SDA high while filtered scl_i remains high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the filtered SDA low-to-high transition is recognized as STOP only while synchronized and filtered SCL is high; busy falls after registered STOP processing and cmd_ack pulses for the STOP command.
elements.check_method: Use the synchronizer/filter reference model to compare sscl, ssda, dsda, sto_condition, busy, scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack. Require STOP qualification and busy clearing only in the filtered-SCL-high window.

elements.stimulus: While busy, drive SDA from low to high while synchronized and filtered scl_i is low, and separately inject a short raw SDA/SCL transition that does not change the filtered SCL value.
elements.expected_response: Contrast case: neither transition is a filtered STOP condition because synchronized and filtered SCL is not high or does not change as required; busy does not clear and no STOP-related cmd_ack is generated.
elements.check_method: Check sto_condition, sscl, ssda, dsda, busy, and cmd_ack against the filtered-edge reference model. Confirm that raw transitions rejected by filtering do not affect STOP status.

elements.stimulus: Issue a READ command with ena=1. During the READ data-bit phase, hold SDA at 0 for one trial and 1 for another before allowing synchronized and filtered scl_i to rise; then complete the low phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the filtered SCL rising edge, dout captures the synchronized and filtered SDA value, respectively 0 or 1, and cmd_ack follows the subsequent low phase.
elements.check_method: Model csda, ssda, dsda, fsda, filtered_scl_rising, and the READ FSM phase. Compare dout's registered update and cmd_ack timing to the model, requiring capture only on the filtered SCL rising edge.

elements.stimulus: Issue a READ command and change SDA while synchronized and filtered scl_i is low, or inject an SDA/SCL raw edge shorter than the filter interval without producing a filtered SCL rising edge; keep the controller in the same READ sampling window.
elements.expected_response: Contrast case: dout does not capture a new value from an SCL level or raw edge that is not a filtered SCL rising edge, and cmd_ack does not advance based on that rejected transition.
elements.check_method: Compare filtered_scl_rising, sscl, ssda, fsda, dout, and cmd_ack with the reference model. Assert that dout changes only when the modeled filtered SCL rising event occurs.

elements.stimulus: With the bus released and ena high, issue a READ command. During the READ data-bit sampling phase, hold the external sda_i line stably low for the complete synchronizer and filter settling interval, then drive or allow a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0032@1: after the filtered SCL rising edge is processed, dout becomes 0, reflecting the filtered-low external SDA value.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage SDA synchronizer, filter sampling, majority filtering, and filtered SCL edge detection; at the modeled filtered SCL rising edge compare the registered dout value with 0 after NBA updates.

elements.stimulus: With the bus released and ena high, issue a READ command. During the READ data-bit sampling phase, hold the external sda_i line stably high for the complete synchronizer and filter settling interval, then drive or allow a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0032@1: after the filtered SCL rising edge is processed, dout becomes 1, reflecting the filtered-high external SDA value.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage SDA synchronizer, filter sampling, majority filtering, and filtered SCL edge detection; at the modeled filtered SCL rising edge compare the registered dout value with 1 after NBA updates.

elements.stimulus: Complete a READ command and record dout after its valid filtered SCL rising-edge sample. After the READ sampling window has ended, toggle the external sda_i line from low to high and back while preventing any new READ sampling phase and any filtered SCL rising edge; also repeat with sda_i changing before a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case of REQ-0032@1: dout does not update from these sda_i changes outside the READ data-bit sampling window or without a filtered SCL rising edge, and retains its previously captured value.
elements.check_method: Monitor the read-sequence and filtered_scl_rising probes, model the registered dout update condition, and assert that dout remains unchanged on every clock where either the READ sampling window is inactive or filtered_scl_rising is not asserted.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Issue cmd=START and allow the START sequence to complete. Then drive sda_i low and hold it stable while scl_i remains high for enough enabled clocks to pass the two-stage synchronizer and three-sample filter.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: ssda changes low only after synchronization and filtering, sta_condition is detected from the filtered transition, and busy asserts after the registered detection update. busy must not assert before the filtered transition.
elements.check_method: Use the ssda, sta_condition, csda, and busy probes; compare busy assertion against a reference model of the two-stage synchronizer and three-sample majority filter, and assert that busy changes only after the modeled filtered SDA high-to-low transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. While the bus is otherwise idle, pulse sda_i low for less than the synchronization/filter acceptance interval, then return it high without allowing a three-sample filtered SDA low value.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: the raw SDA glitch is rejected by synchronization/filtering; ssda does not make a qualifying low transition, sta_condition remains inactive, and busy does not change.
elements.check_method: Monitor csda, fsda, ssda, sta_condition, and busy; use the reference filter model to confirm that the raw pulse does not produce a filtered transition and assert that busy remains at its pre-glitch value.

elements.stimulus: Create a busy transaction by issuing START with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue cmd=WRITE with din=1. During the WRITE stable high phase, when the DUT has released SDA and sda_chk is asserted, externally hold sda_i low long enough to pass synchronization and filtering while scl_i is high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: ssda becomes filtered low during the released-high WRITE phase, arbitration loss is detected, al asserts and remains asserted, the command aborts without cmd_ack, and both scl_oen and sda_oen are released.
elements.check_method: Use write_sequence, sda_chk, csda, fsda, ssda, al, cmd_ack, scl_oen, and sda_oen probes/outputs; compare al timing with the synchronized/filter reference model and assert sticky al, no acknowledgment for the aborted command, and released output enables.

elements.stimulus: Issue START followed by WRITE with din=1, and during the released-high WRITE phase inject an sda_i low pulse shorter than the synchronization/filter acceptance interval, then return sda_i high before ssda becomes low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: the raw SDA pulse does not produce a filtered low value while sda_chk is active; al remains deasserted, the WRITE command is not aborted for arbitration loss, and cmd_ack is eventually produced normally.
elements.check_method: Monitor sda_chk, fsda, ssda, al, write_sequence, cmd_ack, and output enables; use the filter reference model to prove the pulse is rejected and assert no al transition and normal WRITE completion.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue cmd=READ with scl_i initially low, then release/drive scl_i high for the READ high phase and hold sda_i at 1 early enough for the synchronized and filtered SDA value to become high before the filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: ssda reflects the synchronized and filtered high SDA value; on filtered_scl_rising during read_sequence, dout captures 1 after the registered update. dout must correspond to ssda at the filtered SCL rising edge, not to an unsynchronized raw transition.
elements.check_method: Monitor csda, fsda, ssda, filtered_scl_rising, read_sequence, and dout; compare the capture cycle and value with a reference model of synchronization, filtering, and filtered-SCL edge detection.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=READ with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. During the READ high window, toggle sda_i to 1 only briefly and return it to 0 before the synchronization/filter pipeline produces a filtered high value; hold sda_i=0 through the filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: the rejected raw SDA transition does not change ssda to high, and at filtered_scl_rising dout captures the filtered low value 0 rather than the transient raw value 1.
elements.check_method: Monitor csda, fsda, ssda, filtered_scl_rising, read_sequence, and dout; use the reference filter model to confirm no filtered high transition and assert that dout equals ssda at the filtered rising edge and remains unaffected by the raw pulse.

elements.stimulus: With a busy bus, issue cmd=STOP with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. During the STOP sequence, hold scl_i high and drive sda_i from stable low to stable high long enough for synchronization and filtering to complete.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: ssda makes a filtered low-to-high transition while filtered SCL is high, sto_condition is detected, and busy clears after the registered detection update.
elements.check_method: Monitor csda, fsda, ssda, sto_condition, stop_sequence, and busy; compare the busy-clear event with the reference model's filtered SDA transition and assert no clear occurs before that transition.

elements.stimulus: With busy asserted and scl_i high, inject an sda_i high pulse shorter than the synchronization/filter acceptance interval while the filtered SDA remains low, then return sda_i low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: the raw SDA glitch does not create a filtered low-to-high transition, sto_condition remains inactive, and busy remains asserted.
elements.check_method: Monitor csda, fsda, ssda, sto_condition, and busy; compare against the reference filter model and assert that busy is unchanged throughout the rejected pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=START, and keep scl_i and sda_i released high. Drive clocks until the START sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack asserts high for exactly one clk cycle when the START command finishes, then returns low and does not remain high on the next cycle.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model to identify START completion; sample cmd_ack after each posedge and assert a single-cycle high pulse with low values on the preceding and following cycles.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, issue and complete a START command to establish a busy transaction, then set ena=1 and cmd=STOP with scl_i and sda_i released high. Drive clocks until the STOP sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack asserts high for exactly one clk cycle for completion of the STOP command, then returns low without a second-cycle assertion.
elements.check_method: Track command identity and terminal phase in the reference model, distinguish the STOP completion pulse from the earlier START pulse, and compare the observed cmd_ack waveform cycle by cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=READ, and provide a released SDA bus with a valid external SCL high-to-low cycle followed by a filtered SCL rising edge and subsequent low phase. Drive clocks until the READ sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack asserts high for exactly one clk cycle after the READ low phase completes, and is low on all other cycles.
elements.check_method: Model the filtered SCL phases and READ terminal transition, then assert that cmd_ack is a one-cycle pulse aligned with that terminal transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=WRITE, din=0, and provide a released-high bus. Drive clocks through the WRITE SDA setup, released-SCL high phase, and SCL low terminal phase without external arbitration interference.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack asserts high for exactly one clk cycle when the WRITE command finishes, then deasserts on the next clock.
elements.check_method: Use the reference timing model to locate WRITE completion and compare cmd_ack at every clock, requiring one and only one high cycle for this command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=WRITE, din=1, and provide a released-high bus until the WRITE stable-high phase. During that released SDA high phase, externally pull sda_i low and keep it low long enough to pass the filter.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: arbitration loss aborts the WRITE before command completion, so cmd_ack does not produce a one-clock command-complete pulse; it remains low for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: Confirm filtered SDA is low during the din=1 arbitration-check phase, then assert that al becomes active and search the command interval through return to idle for any cmd_ack high cycle; flag any pulse as failure.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=START, clk_cnt=1, and hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 to model a released-high bus. Present START while idle and keep the command inputs stable until the START sequence completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack is asserted high for exactly one clk cycle when the START command finishes, then returns low on the next clk cycle.
