elements.check_method: At every posedge clk, compare cmd_ack against a reference START-sequence model; require one and only one high sample at terminal completion and low on all other sampled cycles.

elements.stimulus: Create a busy transaction by completing a START, then set ena=1, cmd=STOP, clk_cnt=1, and provide a released-high SCL path with no clock stretching. Keep the STOP command applied until its sequence completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack is asserted high for exactly one clk cycle when the STOP command finishes, then returns low.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the STOP phases and compare the registered cmd_ack waveform, checking a single-cycle pulse aligned with STOP terminal completion and no additional pulses.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=READ, clk_cnt=1, hold sda_i=0, and provide released SCL with no stretching. Keep the READ command applied while the controller executes the read bit.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack is asserted high for exactly one clk cycle after the READ low phase completes, then returns low.
elements.check_method: Drive the reference READ timing model and compare cmd_ack after each settled posedge; require exactly one high cycle at command completion and low before and after it.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=WRITE, din=0, clk_cnt=1, and provide a normal released-high SCL response with sda_i following the driven low write bit. Keep the WRITE command applied until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack is asserted high for exactly one clk cycle when the WRITE command finishes, then returns low.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed cmd_ack waveform with a reference WRITE sequence; check that one pulse occurs at the terminal phase and that no high cycles occur before completion or after the following clk.

elements.stimulus: Start an enabled WRITE command with clk_cnt=3 and hold the external bus so the command remains in a nonterminal timing phase for multiple clk cycles before allowing normal completion.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: cmd_ack remains low throughout all command-in-progress cycles before the terminal completion phase; it is not asserted merely because a supported command is active.
elements.check_method: Use the reference FSM to identify every nonterminal cycle and assert cmd_ack==0 on each; separately verify that any later completion pulse is exactly one cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, model an externally valid I2C START by holding filtered SCL high and driving SDA from high to low long enough to pass synchronization and filtering; then observe busy.
elements.expected_response: The busy output asserts after the filtered START is processed; this is the case where busy indicates that the I2C bus is busy.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate synchronization/filter reference model to determine the filtered START-processing cycle, then compare the registered busy output against 1 on that cycle and until a filtered STOP is processed.

elements.stimulus: Starting from the busy state produced by a valid filtered START, hold filtered SCL high and drive SDA from low to high long enough to pass synchronization and filtering, creating a valid I2C STOP; then observe busy.
elements.expected_response: The busy output deasserts after the filtered STOP is processed; this is the contrasting case where busy indicates that the I2C bus is not busy.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate synchronization/filter reference model to determine the filtered STOP-processing cycle, then compare the registered busy output against 0 on that cycle and after it while the bus remains idle.

elements.stimulus: Release both I2C lines and drive SDA high with filtered SCL high, then drive SDA low while keeping SCL high long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to assert sta_condition. After the START detection, keep SDA and SCL stable and do not generate a STOP.
elements.expected_response: The busy port becomes high after the filtered START condition and remains high for every subsequent sampled clock while no filtered STOP condition occurs. This is the holding side of the observed behavior: busy is high after START detection.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, compare busy against a reference model of synchronized three-sample filtering and sta_condition. Require busy to transition low-to-high after sta_condition and remain high until a modeled sto_condition or reset.

elements.stimulus: First create a filtered START by driving SDA high-to-low while filtered SCL is high and wait until busy is high. Then, while filtered SCL remains high, drive SDA low-to-high long enough for filtering to assert sto_condition.
elements.expected_response: busy remains high between the filtered START and filtered STOP, then falls after the filtered STOP condition is detected. This is the contrasting clearing side of the observed behavior: busy falls after STOP detection.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronizer/filter latency and START/STOP edge detection. Sample busy after each posedge and verify it is high after sta_condition, remains high before sto_condition, and transitions high-to-low on the registered response to sto_condition.

elements.stimulus: Release reset, set ena high, issue a WRITE command with din=1, and during the WRITE released-SCL high phase externally hold SDA low while the filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: The DUT detects arbitration loss and asserts al; this is the asserted side of observed_via.shows (al is asserted when arbitration has been lost). al remains asserted after the aborted command until reset, and no command-complete pulse is generated for the aborted WRITE.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after the filtered released-high WRITE phase, compare al with a reference model that detects expected-high SDA versus filtered-low SDA. Check that al becomes 1, remains 1 on subsequent clocks, and that cmd_ack remains 0 for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: Release reset, set ena high, issue a WRITE command with din=0, and let the external bus hold SDA low during the released-SCL high phase; complete the command without any arbitration-loss condition.
elements.expected_response: The DUT keeps al deasserted because arbitration has not been lost; this is the deasserted side of observed_via.shows (al is deasserted when arbitration has not been lost).
elements.check_method: At every posedge throughout the WRITE sequence and after command completion, compare al with the reference model's no-loss state and require al=0; also verify that the normal command-complete pulse occurs.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and release it, set ena=1, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1, and keep the bus otherwise released. When the WRITE sequence reaches its stable SCL-high arbitration-checking phase with sda_oen=1 and sda_chk=1, externally pull SDA low through sda_i=0 while filtered SDA ssda is low.
elements.expected_response: At the arbitration-detection edge, al asserts high. The active WRITE command aborts without producing cmd_ack, and al remains high until reset.
elements.check_method: Use a temporal scoreboard keyed to the sda_chk=1, sda_oen=1, ssda=0 condition; compare the registered al output after the detection posedge, verify no cmd_ack pulse occurs for the aborted command, and verify al remains asserted on subsequent clocks.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and release it, set ena=1, issue a non-STOP command such as cmd=READ, and wait until the command FSM is active. While fsm_active=1 and the filtered SCL is high, drive SDA low and then release it high long enough for the filtered SDA transition to produce sto_condition=1; do not issue a STOP command.
elements.expected_response: When the unexpected filtered STOP is detected during the active non-STOP command, al asserts high and remains asserted until reset. The interrupted command does not complete with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Correlate fsm_active=1 and sto_condition=1 with the next registered al value; require al=1 after that edge, require no cmd_ack for the interrupted command, and check sticky behavior across following clocks.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and release it, set ena=1, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1, and keep SDA externally high throughout the released-SDA arbitration-checking phase so sda_oen=1, sda_chk=1, and filtered SDA ssda=1. Do not create a filtered STOP condition during the active command.
elements.expected_response: al does not newly assert for this active command; it remains low through normal WRITE completion, and the command produces its normal one-clock cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Monitor the arbitration-checking window and filtered STOP detector, then assert that al remains 0 in the absence of either loss condition and that exactly one cmd_ack pulse occurs at normal completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) while idle. Let the FSM reach the READ data-bit window with sda_oen released. Drive the external bus so filtered SDA is 1, then produce a filtered SCL rising edge before the READ command completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at the filtered SCL rising edge during the READ data-bit window, dout captures and presents the received filtered SDA data bit, equal to 1, before cmd_ack is asserted.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered_scl_rising probe and read_sequence probe to identify the scoped sampling event; compare dout after the registering posedge against the filtered SDA/reference-model value and verify the update occurs before the READ cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: Complete an enabled READ command through its data-bit window and wait for cmd_ack. Preserve the resulting dout value, then drive an external SCL transition that produces a filtered SCL rising edge while the FSM is idle and no READ data-bit window is active.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: dout does not capture or change in response to the filtered SCL rising edge outside the READ data-bit window; it retains its previously registered value.
elements.check_method: Use filtered_scl_rising, idle, and read_sequence probes to qualify the edge as outside the READ window; compare dout before and after the registering posedge and require no change, matching the reference model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a READ command while the bus is released, and drive filtered SDA high before the read window's filtered SCL rising edge. Hold SDA high through that edge and allow the read sequence to proceed.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered SCL rising-edge phase, dout updates to 1, the current filtered SDA value. This is the holding case of observed_via.shows: dout captures the current filtered SDA value at the filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model and filtered_scl_rising probe to identify the first filtered SCL rising edge in the READ sequence; sample dout after the corresponding posedge clk and compare it with ssda at that edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a READ command, and drive filtered SDA low so the filtered SCL rising edge captures dout=0. After that edge, while filtered SCL is low and before any subsequent filtered SCL rising edge, change the external SDA so filtered SDA becomes high.
elements.expected_response: dout remains 0 while filtered SDA changes during the non-rising phase; it does not capture the new filtered SDA value until a later filtered SCL rising edge. This is the contrasting case of observed_via.shows: dout does not capture filtered SDA for this requirement at other phases.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered_scl_rising probe and filter reference model to delimit the interval after the capture edge and before the next rising edge; compare dout before and after the filtered SDA transition and require no dout update in that interval.

elements.stimulus: Assert asynchronous nReset, release it, apply synchronous rst, then exercise idle, START, STOP, WRITE, and READ commands with ena high while varying clk_cnt and external SCL/SDA inputs.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: scl_o remains exactly 1'b0 throughout asynchronous reset, synchronous reset, idle operation, and every command-processing phase; scl_oen remains the only DUT-controlled SCL drive signal.
elements.check_method: At every sampled clock and after asynchronous reset changes, compare scl_o against 1'b0 with a concurrent assertion; also confirm that changes in scl_oen or command phase never change scl_o.

elements.stimulus: During reset, idle, and an active command-processing window, inject or force scl_o to 1'b1 for at least one observation sample, then release the injection.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of shows: scl_o has a value other than 1'b0 during the injection, so the requirement is violated and the constant-low scl_o assertion must report a failure; the normal DUT implementation must otherwise return or remain at 1'b0 after the injection is removed.
elements.check_method: Run the same always-low assertion used by the normal check and require it to fail at the injected nonzero sample, while separately checking that the unforced DUT output is 1'b0 before and after injection.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, deassert it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, then issue the START command cmd=0001 for one enabled clock and continue clocking until the START sequence reaches its SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: During the START sequence's SCL-low phase, scl_oen becomes 0 after the corresponding clocked output update; this is the asserted side of the port behavior, indicating that the open-drain control drives SCL low.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, correlate the start_sequence probe with scl_oen and the modeled open-drain SCL line; require scl_oen==0 and the resolved SCL line==0 during the SCL-low phase.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, deassert nReset, apply no command (cmd=0000), keep ena=1, and clock the controller in idle with scl_i and sda_i high.
elements.expected_response: After reset initialization and throughout idle when SCL is not being driven low, scl_oen remains 1; this is the contrasting side of the port behavior, indicating that SCL is released rather than driven low.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen after asynchronous reset settles and after every subsequent posedge while idle; require scl_oen==1 and verify the resolved open-drain SCL line remains high with no external low drive.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, keep the bus externally released high, set ena=1, and issue a START command. Observe the output-control phase before SDA is pulled low and any phase in which SCL is released.
elements.expected_response: Requirement-holds case: scl_oen is 1, which releases SCL for the external pull-up, and sda_o remains constantly 0.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge observation during reset release, idle, and the START SCL-release phase, compare scl_oen to 1 when SCL is released and assert sda_o==0; correlate the released line level with the open-drain bus model.

elements.stimulus: Continue the same enabled START command through the phase after the START condition where the controller pulls SCL low, and then repeat observation during a command phase that drives SCL low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting scl_oen case: scl_oen is 0, which drives SCL low rather than releasing it; sda_o remains constantly 0. This is the 0/drive-low side of the specified scl_oen behavior.
elements.check_method: At settled posedge observations identified by the START-sequence probe, assert scl_oen==0 whenever the controller owns SCL low and assert sda_o==0 at every observation; verify the modeled SCL line is low despite an externally released bus.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena high and a released-high bus, and sample sda_o during the START phase when sda_oen becomes 0 to drive SDA low.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: sda_o is 1'b0 while sda_oen is 0; the module drives SDA low only through the active-low sda_oen control.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge during the SDA-low phase, assert sda_o == 1'b0 and correlate the phase with sda_oen == 0 using a waveform or assertion checker.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command and continue through the phase where the controller releases SDA by setting sda_oen to 1; keep the external SDA line pulled high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of shows: even when sda_oen is 1 and SDA is released to the external pull-up, sda_o remains 1'b0; SDA line control changes through sda_oen, not through sda_o.
elements.check_method: Sample sda_o and sda_oen after each settled posedge across the release phase and assert sda_o == 1'b0 for both sda_oen values, while observing the resolved SDA line become high when released.

elements.stimulus: Release nReset, keep rst low and ena high, provide a released-high SDA/SCL bus, then issue a START command (cmd=0001) and allow the command FSM to reach the SDA-low-while-SCL-high phase.
elements.expected_response: During the START sequence, sda_oen reads 0, which is the asserted active-low SDA drive condition; with the external SDA driver released, the open-drain bus resolves SDA low. This is the 'sda_oen is 0, indicating that SDA is driven low' side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge after the registered output update, monitor the start_sequence probe, sda_oen, and resolved SDA bus value. Assert that the START SDA-low phase has sda_oen==0 and resolved SDA==0; distinguish this from sda_oen==1 release behavior.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, then deassert it while holding rst low, ena high, cmd=0000, and both external bus lines released high; remain in idle without issuing a command.
elements.expected_response: In the reset/idle released-output condition, sda_oen reads 1, so SDA is released rather than driven low. This is the 'sda_oen is 1, indicating that SDA is released rather than driven low' side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Sample sda_oen after asynchronous reset assertion and after settled posedges in idle, while resolving the SDA bus with no external low driver. Assert sda_oen==1 and resolved SDA==1, providing the contrast to the sda_oen==0 drive case.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset, deassert it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the external SDA and SCL lines released high, then issue a START command and sample the initial START-sequence phase after the registered outputs update.
elements.expected_response: The START sequence sets sda_oen=1. This is the release side of observed_via.shows: SDA is released and, with no external low driver, the resolved SDA line is high due to the pull-up.
elements.check_method: At each clock after the START command is accepted, compare sda_oen against the reference FSM phase and resolve SDA as low only when sda_oen=0 or an external participant drives low; require sda_oen=1 and resolved SDA=1 during the release phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset and a completed START, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a WRITE command with din=0, and wait for the WRITE data-drive phase with the external participant not driving SDA.
elements.expected_response: The WRITE sequence sets sda_oen=0. This is the otherwise side of observed_via.shows: SDA is driven low rather than released, and the resolved SDA line is low.
elements.check_method: At the WRITE data-drive phase, compare sda_oen with the reference command phase and resolve SDA from the open-drain model; require sda_oen=0 and resolved SDA=0, contrasting with the release case.

elements.stimulus: Provide the finalized specification artifact to the requirements/documentation checker.
elements.expected_response: The specification contains an implementation-details section introduced at the required location and does not omit that section.
elements.check_method: Perform a structural and textual artifact check that locates the heading or section beginning with "Implementation details:" and compare its presence and ordering against the specification source.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous and synchronous reset, then operate the controller through idle, START, WRITE with din=0 and din=1, READ, and STOP phases with ena high; vary external SCL and SDA between low and released-high conditions while monitoring scl_o and sda_o after every clocked update.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: scl_o remains 0 and sda_o remains 0 during reset, idle, and every command phase, regardless of output-enable state or external bus level. The controller may release or pull lines low only through scl_oen and sda_oen; it never drives either line high directly.
elements.check_method: At every sampled clock after reset and throughout each exercised phase, assert scl_o == 1'b0 and sda_o == 1'b0; independently reconstruct bus levels from the external drivers and output enables to ensure a high bus level is not attributed to scl_o or sda_o.

elements.stimulus: Run the same reset and command-phase sequence against a fault-injected DUT variant in which either scl_o or sda_o is assigned 1 during at least one reset or operating phase, while keeping the external open-drain bus model active.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise side of shows: any sampled scl_o == 1 indicates that the module drives SCL high directly, and any sampled sda_o == 1 indicates that the module drives SDA high directly; the checker must report REQ-0049@1 as failed for either violation.
elements.check_method: Use assertions sampled after each clocked update, including asynchronous-reset observations: assert scl_o == 0 and sda_o == 0. Deliberately confirm that the injected high value triggers a failing assertion and is distinguished from an externally pulled-high bus caused by released output enables.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset asynchronously, then deassert it; apply synchronous rst for one posedge, and observe scl_o and sda_o both during reset and after returning to idle.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_o and sda_o are continuously low (1'b0) during reset and idle observation; this is the `shows` side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: At asynchronous reset assertion, the following posedge, and multiple settled samples after reset release, compare both output ports against 1'b0 with an always-on assertion.

elements.stimulus: With rst and nReset inactive, drive clk_cnt values 0, 1, and 16'hffff; issue START, WRITE with din=0, WRITE with din=1, READ, and STOP commands with ena high, while varying scl_i and sda_i and allowing each sequence to run to completion.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: during every command phase and every externally observable clock, scl_o and sda_o must remain low. Any non-low value would be the `otherwise`/non-holding side (`scl_o` or `sda_o` is not low) and is a failure; command activity must not alter the constant assignments.
elements.check_method: Use a concurrent assertion sampled on every clock and after each command/output update that scl_o==1'b0 and sda_o==1'b0, including all prescaler values, command transitions, and bus-response variations.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low between clock edges, release it, and keep rst low, ena high, and both external SCL and SDA drivers released. Observe the initialized idle interval.
elements.expected_response: This is the released side of shows: scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, and with no external low driver the SCL and SDA lines remain high rather than being pulled low.
elements.check_method: After asynchronous reset settles, sample scl_oen, sda_oen, and the modeled open-drain bus lines. Assert that each line is high exactly when its corresponding output enable is high and all external drivers are released.

elements.stimulus: With the bus released high, ena high, and a valid prescaler, issue a START command and wait for the START sequence to reach the phase that pulls SDA low while SCL remains released high.
elements.expected_response: This is the pulled-low side of shows for SDA: sda_oen=0 and the modeled SDA line is low. SCL remains released with scl_oen=1 and a high modeled SCL line.
elements.check_method: At the registered START output phase after the relevant posedge, compare sda_oen and scl_oen with the open-drain bus model. Assert that SDA is low when sda_oen is low and SCL is high when scl_oen is high with no external low driver.

elements.stimulus: Continue the valid START command sequence from the SDA-low/SCL-high phase until the controller pulls SCL low, with the external bus otherwise released.
elements.expected_response: This is the pulled-low side of shows for SCL: scl_oen=0 and the modeled SCL line is low. The SDA output state remains the state commanded by the START phase.
elements.check_method: Sample the registered output enables and modeled bus lines after each posedge. Assert that the SCL line is low whenever scl_oen is low, independent of the constant scl_o output value.

elements.stimulus: Complete a START transaction, then issue a STOP command with ena high and no external participant pulling either line low. Wait through the STOP sequence until SCL is released high and SDA is released high.
elements.expected_response: This is the released side of shows after active driving: scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, and the modeled SCL and SDA lines are high because neither corresponding enable pulls its line low.
elements.check_method: Monitor the STOP output phases after registered updates. Assert that each released output enable is high and that the open-drain bus model reports the corresponding line high when external drivers are released.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and clk_cnt set to a finite nonzero value, issue a STOP command and let the STOP sequence progress through the phase where SCL is released high and SDA is then released while SCL remains high. Model the external bus with no external low drive so a released line can rise through the pull-up.
elements.expected_response: During the STOP sequence's released-SDA phase, sda_oen is 1, indicating that SDA is released for the external pull-up to provide the high level; the observed SDA bus line is high.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after registered outputs settle, compare sda_oen against the reference STOP phase model and sample the modeled SDA bus value. Bin observation of sda_oen=1 with SDA high during the released-SDA phase.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and clk_cnt set to a finite nonzero value, issue a STOP command and observe the initial STOP phase before SCL is released, when the controller must ensure SDA is low. Model the bus with the DUT as the only low driver.
elements.expected_response: During the initial STOP phase, sda_oen is 0, indicating that SDA is actively pulled low rather than released for the external pull-up; the observed SDA bus line is low. This is the contrasting, non-holding side of the observed_via shows condition.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after registered outputs settle, compare sda_oen against the reference STOP phase model and sample the modeled SDA bus value. Bin observation of sda_oen=0 with SDA low before the STOP release phase.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate and run the DUT in a nominal idle configuration, including reset release and no-op command activity, while reaching the specification context corresponding to list item 2.
elements.expected_response: No REQ-0053-specific output behavior is required; the DUT remains subject only to behaviors covered by other requirements.
elements.check_method: Traceability review: confirm the test contains no assertion or scoreboard obligation attributable to REQ-0053 beyond recording that its specification item was exercised.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to 16'h003A, hold ena high, then assert nReset low asynchronously between clock edges and keep it low across a posedge; afterward deassert nReset and assert rst high for one posedge.
elements.expected_response: While nReset is active, and on the posedge with rst active, cnt loads 16'h003A and clk_en is asserted. This is the reset-active side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a reference divider model sampled after asynchronous reset changes and after the relevant posedge; compare the cnt probe to clk_cnt and require clk_en=1 during both reset conditions.

elements.stimulus: Deassert both resets, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0025, arrange the divider counter to contain 16'h0000 at a posedge, and keep scl_i high so no clock-synchronization event occurs.
elements.expected_response: When cnt reaches zero, cnt reloads to 16'h0025 and clk_en is asserted. This is the counter-expiry side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: At the posedge where cnt_zero is observed, compare the post-update cnt probe with clk_cnt and check that clk_en is a one-clock assertion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set clk_cnt=16'h0017 and ena=0 for several consecutive posedges, then set ena=1 while retaining a nonzero counter reload value.
elements.expected_response: On each disabled-clock posedge, cnt loads 16'h0017 and clk_en is asserted rather than allowing normal countdown. This is the core-disabled side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor cnt and clk_en on every posedge while ena=0; require cnt==clk_cnt and clk_en==1 for each disabled cycle, then verify normal enabled operation resumes after ena becomes high.

elements.stimulus: Run with ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0020 until the controller has released SCL high, then drive scl_i low long enough to produce a filtered SCL falling event and scl_sync=1 while the counter is nonzero.
elements.expected_response: When multi-master clock synchronization occurs, cnt reloads 16'h0020 and clk_en is asserted. This is the synchronization side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered SCL and scl_sync probes to identify the synchronization cycle, then compare the post-update cnt probe with clk_cnt and require clk_en=1 on that cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0005, keep scl_i stable so scl_sync=0, and start with cnt=16'h0004; observe several enabled posedges without allowing cnt to reach zero.
elements.expected_response: Because reset, cnt_zero, ena-low, and synchronization are all inactive, cnt decrements according to the divider and clk_en remains deasserted until expiry. This is the non-holding side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge before expiry, compare cnt against a reference countdown model and require clk_en=0; separately verify that no reload occurs while the activation conditions are absent.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep rst low, set ena high and clk_cnt to a nonzero value such as 3. Issue a supported START command while scl_i and sda_i are released high, then keep ena high with reset inactive and avoid external SCL stretching or clock-synchronization transitions throughout the active timing phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the requirement: with no counter-reload condition, the internal counter decrements on every clk cycle. scl_oen remains in the current phase for the programmed countdown and then advances to the next prescribed START timing phase when the counter expires; no extra cycles are inserted.
elements.check_method: Use the reference divider model to predict each countdown and expiry from clk_cnt=3. At each posedge compare the observed registered scl_oen phase progression against the model, checking that the phase transition occurs after the expected number of cycles rather than being delayed.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep rst low, set ena high and clk_cnt to a nonzero value such as 3, and issue a supported START command. After the command enters an active timing phase but before the countdown expires, drive ena low for two clk cycles, then drive ena high again while keeping reset inactive and the external bus released.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case of the requirement: while ena is low, the counter does not decrement because a reload condition applies. scl_oen remains in its current timing phase and the expected phase transition is delayed by the disabled interval; after ena returns high, countdown resumes from the reloaded timing value.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_oen phase-transition timing with a reference model that reloads rather than decrements on each ena-low cycle. Confirm that no phase advance occurs during the two disabled cycles and that the subsequent transition is later than in the continuously enabled case by the corresponding reload/countdown delay.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4, issue a supported START command, and model the bus as high until the START sequence releases SCL. Immediately thereafter externally hold scl_i low long enough for filtered SCL (sscl) to become 0 and slave_wait to assert; keep scl_i low for multiple enabled-clock periods.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the requirement: while slave_wait=1, the timing counter retains its pre-wait value, clk_en remains low on every clock, the released SCL output enable remains scl_oen=1, the active command does not advance, and cmd_ack does not pulse during the stretch.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered updates settle, use a scoreboard to compare the filter/slave-wait reference model with slave_wait and sscl, assert that the sampled timing-counter value is unchanged from entry and clk_en=0 throughout the wait, and assert no cmd_ack pulse until after scl_i is released and filtered SCL becomes high.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4, issue the same supported START command, and keep the externally released SCL line high so filtered SCL remains high when the command reaches its released-SCL phase; do not apply clock stretching.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case of the requirement: slave_wait remains 0, the timing counter proceeds to expiration, clk_en asserts at the modeled timing ticks, the FSM advances through the command phases, and cmd_ack eventually pulses once.
elements.check_method: Compare sscl and slave_wait against the bus/filter reference model, verify counter progression and clk_en timing against the divider model, and use a one-clock-pulse assertion plus a completion scoreboard to confirm that cmd_ack occurs rather than being postponed by a wait state.

elements.stimulus: Encounter the specification list-item marker "3."; apply no command, bus, reset, or enable stimulus attributable to this item.
elements.expected_response: No DUT output behavior, state transition, timing constraint, or functional result is required or inferred for this item.
elements.check_method: Review the generated verification traceability and testbench assertions to confirm this item has no functional stimulus or expected-output assertion beyond its presence in the coverage map.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low then release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4, issue a supported WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=0, and hold scl_i low externally through the WRITE phase after the DUT releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1). Keep scl_i low long enough for synchronization and filtering to make sscl=0.
elements.expected_response: REQ-0058 holding case: while scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL sscl remains 0, slave_wait is asserted; the timing counter and command FSM remain paused and do not advance to the next high-phase command state.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge of clk, compare scl_oen, sscl, slave_wait, clk_en, and the command-state probe against a reference model. Assert that every interval with scl_oen=1 and sscl=0 has slave_wait=1, clk_en=0, and no FSM phase advance.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low then release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4, issue a supported WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=0, and allow scl_i to remain high externally when the DUT releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1). Keep scl_i high long enough for synchronization and filtering to make sscl=1.
elements.expected_response: REQ-0058 non-holding case: when scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL sscl=1, slave_wait is not asserted; the controller may generate clk_en and advance the WRITE sequence according to the prescaler.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge of clk, compare scl_oen, sscl, slave_wait, clk_en, and the command-state probe against a reference model. Assert that the released-and-filtered-high interval has slave_wait=0 and that timing/FSM progression is not suppressed by slave-wait logic.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue a READ command with the bus initially high. When the READ sequence releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1), externally hold scl_i low long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to settle.
elements.expected_response: While the master has released SCL, scl_oen remains 1 and the filtered SCL probe sscl becomes and remains 0, indicating that a slave or another bus participant is holding SCL low. The controller must not treat SCL as high until the filtered input becomes high.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after the READ sequence reaches the SCL-release phase, compare scl_oen and sscl against a reference model of the two-stage synchronizer and three-sample majority filter; require scl_oen=1 and sscl=0 throughout the externally held-low interval.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue a READ command with scl_i held high by the external bus. When the READ sequence releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1), continue driving the external bus high and allow the filter to settle.
elements.expected_response: When the master has released SCL and no external participant holds it low, scl_oen is 1 and the filtered SCL probe sscl becomes 1. This is the contrasting non-holding case to the requirement's indication sscl=0.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after the READ sequence reaches the SCL-release phase, compare scl_oen and sscl against the synchronizer/filter reference model; require scl_oen=1 and sscl=1 after the modeled filter settling interval.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0, and model the external bus so SCL is held low after the controller releases it (scl_oen=1). Keep the external SCL low for multiple enabled clocks, then release it high and continue clocking.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: while slave_wait=1 and filtered SCL sscl=0, scl_oen remains 1 throughout the stretch; the timing counter and FSM do not advance to the next SCL phase. After filtered SCL becomes high, timing resumes and subsequent progression may pull scl_oen low.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_oen, slave_wait, cnt_zero, and clk_en against a reference model of clock stretching. Assert that no scl_oen falling transition or command-phase advance occurs while slave_wait=1 and sscl=0, and that progression resumes after sscl=1.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue the same supported WRITE command with din=0, and leave the external SCL released high whenever scl_oen=1 so filtered SCL sscl reaches high without clock stretching. Continue clocking through the released-SCL phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: because filtered SCL is released high, slave_wait does not remain active; the timing counter continues, and scl_oen advances to the next SCL phase by falling low rather than remaining high indefinitely.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to predict the enabled timing ticks and phase transitions. Check that sscl=1 while SCL is released, slave_wait is deasserted, clk_en continues to occur, and scl_oen eventually falls low at the expected phase without waiting for an external low-to-high transition.

elements.stimulus: Apply no requirement-specific stimulus; leave the DUT in its normal initialized condition.
elements.expected_response: No requirement-specific DUT behavior is mandated by REQ-0061.
elements.check_method: Review the requirement-to-testplan trace and confirm that REQ-0061 declares no behavioral obligation, observable output, activation condition, or interface effect; record the scenario as intentionally non-operational.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a stable-high bus, issue a valid WRITE command and wait until the controller releases SCL (scl_oen=1) during its high phase. Keep scl_i high long enough for the filtered SCL to be high, then externally pull scl_i low and hold it low long enough for the filter to register a filtered SCL falling edge.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered SCL falling edge occurs while scl_oen is 1, scl_sync asserts; this is the 'requirement holds' side of the observation.
elements.check_method: Use the synchronized/filter reference model to predict the cycle of the filtered SCL falling edge, then compare the sampled scl_sync probe at that cycle against 1 and verify it is not asserted before the predicted edge.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a stable-high bus, issue a valid WRITE command and wait until the controller releases SCL (scl_oen=1) during its high phase. Keep scl_i high continuously for several filter sampling intervals, with no external SCL transition that can produce a filtered falling edge.
elements.expected_response: scl_sync remains deasserted throughout the released-high interval because the filtered SCL does not fall; this is the 'requirement does not hold' side of the observation.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to confirm that filtered SCL remains high, and assert that scl_sync is 0 on every sampled clock during the interval, including the cycle corresponding to the absence of a filtered falling edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and scl_oen=1 so the controller has released SCL. Drive scl_i high long enough for the filtered SCL sscl to be high, then have an external master pull scl_i low and hold it long enough for the filter to produce a falling edge on sscl.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered SCL falling edge is processed while scl_oen=1, scl_sync asserts, indicating the holding case of shows: another master has forced SCL low.
elements.check_method: Use the sscl probe and the filter reference model to identify the filtered falling-edge cycle; sample scl_sync after the corresponding posedge and require it to assert on that cycle, with a coverage bin for the released-SCL filtered-falling condition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and scl_oen=1 so the controller has released SCL. Keep scl_i high and stable for multiple filter sampling intervals, without any filtered SCL falling edge.
elements.expected_response: scl_sync remains deasserted, indicating the non-holding case of shows: no other master has forced SCL low.
elements.check_method: Monitor sscl with the filter reference model to confirm no filtered falling edge occurs, then compare scl_sync after every enabled posedge and require it to remain 0 throughout the observation window.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4, keep the bus released high, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0, and wait for the command's released-SCL high phase as indicated by scl_oen=1 and the active WRITE phase. While scl_oen remains 1, drive scl_i low externally to represent another master forcing SCL low, then release scl_i high after at least one timing interval.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: scl_oen remains released during the externally forced synchronized low period and does not proceed at the locally scheduled phase boundary; after the timing counter is reloaded and the restarted low-period interval completes, scl_oen changes at the subsequent SCL phase boundary.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate divider/FSM reference model and waveform assertions to detect the released-SCL phase, the external scl_i falling edge, and the resulting scl_oen transition. Confirm the transition is delayed by the synchronization-induced counter reload/restarted low-period interval relative to the locally scheduled boundary, and optionally correlate the delay with scl_sync and cnt_zero probes.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4, keep scl_i and sda_i high, issue the same supported WRITE command with din=0, and wait for its released-SCL high phase as indicated by scl_oen=1 and the active WRITE phase. Do not introduce any external SCL falling edge; keep scl_i high through the locally scheduled low-period timing and phase boundary.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case of shows: without an external SCL falling edge while SCL is released, scl_oen changes at the locally scheduled phase boundary after the local timing interval, with no synchronization-induced timing restart or additional delay.
elements.check_method: Compare the scl_oen waveform against the same cycle-accurate reference model and against TP-0000's baseline interval. Assert that no scl_sync event or counter-reload-induced extension occurs and that the phase transition occurs at the locally scheduled boundary.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it, keep rst low and ena high, then drive scl_i and sda_i to stable low values for at least three rising edges of clk followed by stable high values for at least three more rising edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: cscl and csda initially reflect the reset-high synchronization state, then each raw scl_i and sda_i value appears at the corresponding probe only after propagation through the two-stage synchronization path, with no missed or spurious synchronized value while the raw inputs remain stable.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare cscl and csda against a cycle-accurate two-stage reference model loaded with scl_i and sda_i; require the probes to match the second-stage model and verify both low and high transitions.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold scl_i and sda_i high, then change both raw inputs to low immediately before a rising edge of clk and keep them low; sample cscl and csda after that edge and after the next edge before allowing the two-stage capture to complete.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of shows: cscl and csda do not directly follow the newly changed raw inputs on the first capture edge or otherwise bypass the two-stage path; they retain the prior synchronized value until the reference model's second synchronization stage receives the low samples, after which they become low.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate two-register synchronizer model and compare cscl/csda after every settled posedge, specifically checking that the first and second intermediate observations do not equal an immediate combinational copy of the raw transition and that the eventual second-stage value is correct.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it, then keep rst low and ena high. Set clk_cnt to a nonzero value such as 8. Drive stable raw scl_i and sda_i values that produce known synchronized samples, then run fewer enabled clocks than the filter-counter expiry interval while changing the synchronized input values before the next permitted sampling event.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding side of the observed difference: while the filter counter has not expired, filter_cnt remains non-expired and the synchronized samples are not shifted into fSCL or fSDA; fscl and fsda retain their previous history contents.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset settling, compare filter_cnt, fscl, and fsda against a reference model of the filter counter and two-stage synchronizer. Bin cycles with filter_cnt nonzero and assert that fscl/fsda do not perform a history shift on those cycles.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it, then keep rst low and ena high. Set clk_cnt to a nonzero value such as 8. Drive stable scl_i and sda_i values, allow the two-stage synchronizers to capture them, and run through successive enabled clocks until filter_cnt expires; repeat with a changed pair of synchronized input values for a later filter-counter expiration.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of the observed difference: whenever filter_cnt expires, the current synchronized SCL and SDA samples are shifted into the three-sample histories, so fscl and fsda update exactly at the permitted sampling events and remain unchanged between those events.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the synchronizers, filter-counter reload/expiry, and three-sample history shift. At each expiration, compare fscl/fsda with the model's shifted histories; on non-expiration cycles, assert no history shift.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 so filtering samples on every enabled clock. Drive scl_i and sda_i through the synchronizer so the sampled three-history values become fscl=3'b110 and fsda=3'b110, then hold the lines long enough for the histories and filtered outputs to settle. Also exercise the complementary newest-sample pattern fscl=3'b011 and fsda=3'b011.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when each three-sample history contains two highs and one low, sscl and ssda are high, including when the newest sample is low (110). The complementary history with the newest sample high (011) also produces high. This is the majority-value side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: At each filter update, use a reference model that shifts the synchronized samples into fscl and fsda and computes (h0 & h1) | (h0 & h2) | (h1 & h2). Compare sscl and ssda with the model after registered updates, and verify both outputs remain high for 110 and 011 histories.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 so filtering samples on every enabled clock. Drive scl_i and sda_i through the synchronizer so the sampled three-history values become fscl=3'b001 and fsda=3'b001, then hold the lines long enough for the histories and filtered outputs to settle. Also exercise the complementary newest-sample pattern fscl=3'b100 and fsda=3'b100.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: when each three-sample history contains only one high and two lows, sscl and ssda are low, including when the newest sample is high (001). The complementary history with the newest sample low (100) also produces low. This is the non-majority side of the observed behavior and demonstrates that the filtered outputs do not simply follow the newest or current sample.
elements.check_method: At each filter update, compute the three-input majority from the observed fscl and fsda histories with (h0 & h1) | (h0 & h2) | (h1 & h2). Compare sscl and ssda against the computed low result for 001 and 100, and specifically flag any output that follows the newest sample instead of the majority.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1, drive scl_i low for one enabled sampling interval and then return it high, while keeping sda_i high. Allow the synchronizer and three-sample filter to process the pulse.

elements.expected_response: Holding case of the requirement: the short SDA glitch has a reduced effect; ssda remains high because the three-sample majority history does not contain a low majority, and sscl remains high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive scl_i high and sda_i high long enough for synchronization and the three-sample filter to settle. Then drive sda_i low while keeping scl_i high for at least the filter interval, allowing the filtered SDA value to transition from high to low.
elements.expected_response: The filtered SDA falling transition occurs while filtered SCL is high, so sta_condition asserts for the detected START condition. This is the positive side of the required behavior: the port indicates START when the condition holds.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage synchronizers, filter sampling, three-sample majority, and delayed filtered SDA. At the modeled filtered SDA high-to-low transition with filtered SCL high, compare the sta_condition probe against 1 and verify it does not assert before the filtered transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive scl_i low and sda_i high long enough for synchronization and the three-sample filter to settle. Then drive sda_i low while keeping scl_i low for at least the filter interval, allowing the filtered SDA value to transition from high to low without filtered SCL being high.
elements.expected_response: Because the filtered SDA fall occurs while filtered SCL is low, sta_condition remains deasserted. This is the negative side of the required behavior: the port does not indicate START when the qualifying SCL-high condition does not hold.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to identify the filtered SDA high-to-low transition and confirm filtered SCL is 0 at that point; compare sta_condition over the transition and subsequent enabled clocks against 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=0 long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce sscl=1 and ssda=0. Then drive sda_i=1 while keeping scl_i=1 long enough for the filtered SDA transition to become ssda=0 followed by ssda=1, with sscl remaining high.
elements.expected_response: The filtered SDA rising transition while filtered SCL is high causes sto_condition to assert, indicating an I2C STOP condition has been detected. This is the asserting side of the port observation.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage synchronizers, filter history, majority filtering, and delayed filtered SDA. At the cycle where the model predicts ssda=1, prior dSDA=0, and sscl=1, compare the sto_condition probe against 1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. First drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=0 long enough for filtered sscl=1 and ssda=0. Then drive scl_i=0 and keep it low until filtered sscl=0, while changing sda_i from 0 to 1 and holding both inputs long enough for filtered ssda to rise.
elements.expected_response: The filtered SDA rising transition does not assert sto_condition because filtered SCL is low. This is the non-asserting side of the port observation.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to identify the cycle in which ssda rises while sscl=0, and verify sto_condition remains 0 on that cycle and does not produce a STOP indication from this transition.

elements.stimulus: Perform a requirements-to-testplan audit for list item 7 without applying any additional DUT stimulus or assigning a functional behavior to REQ-0072.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1 for sufficient enabled clocks to establish filtered high levels. Drive sda_i low while keeping scl_i high and hold it low long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce a filtered SDA falling edge. Then drive sda_i high while keeping scl_i high and hold it long enough for a filtered SDA rising edge.
elements.expected_response: The busy output is low before the filtered START, rises at the registered response to the filtered START condition, remains high throughout the interval after START and before the filtered STOP, and returns low at the registered response to the filtered STOP condition. This is the holding case of the requirement: busy is set by START and remains set until STOP.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the synchronizers, filter history, filtered SDA/SCL transitions, and registered busy update. At each settled posedge compare busy with the model and assert high on every cycle between the modeled START and STOP response edges, with exactly the specified registered observation latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1 for sufficient enabled clocks without producing a filtered SDA falling edge. Then produce a valid filtered START by driving sda_i low while scl_i remains high, followed by a valid filtered STOP by driving sda_i high while scl_i remains high; continue holding both lines high afterward.
elements.expected_response: The busy output remains low before the filtered START, becomes high only after the filtered START is detected, and becomes low after the filtered STOP is detected and remains low afterward. The pre-START and post-STOP low behavior is the contrasting side of the requirement's observation: busy is low before START and after STOP.
elements.check_method: Compare settled registered busy samples against a reference model of filtered START/STOP detection. Assert busy=0 during the pre-START interval and every cycle after the modeled STOP response edge; also ensure no busy transition occurs from the stable high bus without a filtered START or STOP event.

elements.stimulus: Encounter numbered item 8 while reviewing the specification; apply no DUT stimulus and make no assumption about any command, reset, or bus state.
elements.expected_response: No specific DUT output, state transition, timing, or protocol behavior is required by this item.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a WRITE command (cmd=0100) with din=1, and model the bus so that when sda_oen=1 and sda_chk=1 during the stable high phase, the external participant drives sda_i low long enough for the filtered SDA probe ssda to become 0.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE stable-high arbitration phase, sda_oen=1, sda_chk=1, and ssda=0; al asserts on the corresponding registered update and remains asserted until reset. The command is aborted and both output enables are released; no completion acknowledgement is generated for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, monitor sda_oen, sda_chk, ssda, al, cmd_ack, and both output enables. Assert that al becomes 1 while sda_oen=1, sda_chk=1, and ssda=0, then remains 1 until reset, and that no cmd_ack occurs for this command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a WRITE command (cmd=0100) with din=1, and leave the external bus released high so sda_i remains high and the filtered SDA probe ssda remains 1 throughout the stable high arbitration-checking phase.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE stable-high phase, sda_oen=1 and sda_chk=1 but ssda=1; al does not assert due to the absent SDA-low arbitration condition, and the WRITE proceeds without arbitration-loss indication.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, identify the phase where write_sequence, sda_chk, and sda_oen are active and compare ssda with al. Assert that ssda remains 1 and al remains 0 throughout that phase and until normal command completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a valid READ command, and wait until read_sequence and fsm_active are high with filtered SCL high. Drive the external SDA line low and then high long enough for the three-sample filter to produce a filtered SDA low-to-high transition while filtered SCL remains high, asserting sto_condition during the active non-STOP command.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the observed behavior: al rises on the detected filtered STOP, remains asserted, the active READ command aborts without generating cmd_ack, and both scl_oen and sda_oen are released.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronizer, filter, filtered STOP detection, and FSM timing. At the cycle where sto_condition rises while fsm_active is high and cmd is READ, compare al against a rising sticky flag; verify no cmd_ack is produced for the aborted command and verify both output enables are 1 after abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al low, establish a busy transaction, issue the requested STOP command with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, and allow the STOP sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL high, then release SDA high while SCL is high so that sto_condition is detected during the STOP command.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case of the observed behavior: because the active command is the requested STOP command, al does not newly rise when sto_condition is detected; the STOP command completes with its normal one-clock cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd, stop_sequence, sto_condition, al, and cmd_ack with a cycle-accurate reference model. Assert that al remains 0 through the filtered STOP event and that exactly one cmd_ack pulse occurs at normal STOP completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al low, leave the FSM idle with ena=1 and cmd=NOP. Drive the external bus through a filtered STOP transition by holding filtered SCL high and causing filtered SDA to transition low then high long enough to assert sto_condition, without issuing a command.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting inactive-FSM case of the observed behavior: sto_condition while fsm_active is low does not newly assert al, and the FSM remains idle with no command-complete pulse.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered-line reference model to identify the cycle sto_condition rises while idle is high. Compare al before and after that cycle, requiring no rising edge, and check that idle remains high and cmd_ack remains low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a WRITE command with ena high and din=1. Allow the controller to enter the stable high WRITE phase with sda_chk asserted, then externally hold SDA low while the DUT has released SDA high; keep SCL available high until arbitration loss is detected.
elements.expected_response: At the edge where al rises to 1, the requirement holds: the FSM returns to idle and both scl_oen and sda_oen are high, releasing SCL and SDA. No command-complete pulse is generated for the aborted WRITE.
elements.check_method: At the sampled posedge where al transitions from 0 to 1, compare scl_oen==1, sda_oen==1, and idle==1; verify cmd_ack==0 on that edge and subsequent command-abort cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a WRITE command with ena high and din=0. During the stable high WRITE phase, externally hold SDA low, matching the DUT's intended low data value, and allow the command to proceed normally.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting otherwise side of the observation applies: no arbitration-loss indication occurs, al remains 0, and the controller does not return to idle or release both lines as an arbitration-loss response. During the active WRITE high phase, sda_oen remains low for din=0 while scl_oen is high; the command eventually completes with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Monitor the complete WRITE sequence and verify al never asserts, fsm_active/write_sequence remains active through the high phase, sda_oen==0 while din=0 is driven, and cmd_ack asserts at normal completion; specifically confirm there is no al-rising edge accompanied by both output enables high.

elements.stimulus: Perform a requirements-to-testplan audit of numbered item 9; apply no DUT stimulus because the item specifies no activation condition, boundary effect, or behavioral expectation.

elements.check_method: Review the traceability record and confirm that the testplan does not impose any additional DUT expectation beyond documenting that REQ-0078 is non-behavioral scaffolding.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and use clk_cnt=0 for sampling on every enabled clock. Drive the external bus so synchronized and filtered SCL samples produce a low-to-high majority transition, while synchronized and filtered SDA samples are stable at 1 before the transition. Issue a READ command and continue clocking until the filtered_scl_rising probe asserts.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: on the clock processing the filtered SCL rising edge, dout becomes 1, equal to the current filtered SDA value ssda.
elements.check_method: At every assertion of filtered_scl_rising, sample ssda and compare it with dout after the same posedge's registered outputs settle; require equality and record a coverage bin for filtered SDA=1.

elements.stimulus: Initialize dout to 0, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold filtered SCL low, and drive synchronized/filter samples to change filtered SDA from 0 to 1 without allowing filtered SCL to rise. Clock through the filter update and verify that filtered_scl_rising remains deasserted; then keep SCL low for additional clocks.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise side of shows: because no filtered SCL rising edge occurs, dout does not capture the new filtered SDA value; dout remains 0 rather than becoming 1.
elements.check_method: Assert that filtered_scl_rising is never asserted during the SDA-only transition and compare dout after each settled posedge against its pre-transition value; require dout to remain 0 while ssda is 1 and SCL has not produced a filtered rising edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (1000). During the READ data-sampling window, release SDA and drive the external bus so filtered SDA is 0, then produce one filtered SCL rising edge; repeat with filtered SDA equal to 1 and produce a second filtered SCL rising edge, allowing the operation to reach its normal completion.
elements.expected_response: On each filtered SCL rising edge during the READ data-sampling window, dout updates to and presents the corresponding filtered SDA value (0 for the first bit and 1 for the second bit) for collection by the byte-level controller. This is the holding side of the observed_via shows condition.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for synchronization, filtering, filtered_scl_rising, and registered dout timing. At each modeled filtered SCL rising edge in read_sequence, compare dout after the capturing posedge with the modeled filtered SDA value and verify the value remains available until the next captured bit or reset.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=READ with ena=1, release SDA, and hold filtered SCL low for several enabled timing ticks so no filtered SCL rising edge occurs; then terminate or abort the operation before any filtered SCL rising edge, using reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: While no filtered SCL rising edge occurs in the READ data-sampling window, dout does not present a new filtered SDA sample as a received READ data bit; it retains its previously registered value. This is the contrasting, non-holding side of the observed_via shows condition.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to prove that filtered_scl_rising remains low throughout the interval. Sample dout after every enabled posedge and assert that it does not change to the current SDA value solely because time advances; also verify reset or arbitration loss ends the operation without a new READ-bit capture.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, set clk_cnt=1, and present cmd=START while the FSM is idle. Hold the command and inputs stable through the timing interval until an internal clk_en tick occurs.
elements.expected_response: Advances side of the contrast: on an enabled clk_en assertion, the command FSM leaves idle and enters the START command sequence; the observed state probes show the corresponding idle-to-start_sequence transition only at that timing-enable event.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, sample clk_en and the idle/start_sequence probes after registered updates settle. Assert that any idle-to-start_sequence transition is coincident with clk_en=1, and that a clk_en=1 tick during valid START acceptance produces the expected transition.

elements.stimulus: Begin with ena=1 and accept cmd=START on a clk_en tick so the FSM is active in the START sequence. Before the next timing tick, drive ena=0 and hold it low for multiple rising clock edges while keeping the bus and command inputs stable.
elements.expected_response: Holds side of the contrast: while clk_en is not asserted, the command FSM remains in the same START-sequence state; idle, fsm_active, start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence probes show no command-FSM state transition during the ena=0 interval.
elements.check_method: Record the command-FSM state probes on each posedge and compare consecutive samples during cycles with clk_en=0. Assert state equality across every such cycle, including the multi-cycle ena=0 interval, and flag any transition without a coincident clk_en=1.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, scl_i=1, sda_i=1, and cmd=4'b0001 (START). Hold cmd and ena through the next enabled clock tick while idle.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the enabled idle command-acceptance tick, the FSM enters start_sequence; start_sequence becomes observable and the START output phase begins, with no entry into stop_sequence, read_sequence, or write_sequence.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset, compare the start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence probes against a reference FSM model and verify that start_sequence is the first active sequence after the clk_en tick.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, scl_i=1, sda_i=1, and cmd=4'b0010 (STOP). Hold cmd and ena through the next enabled clock tick while idle.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the enabled idle command-acceptance tick, the FSM enters stop_sequence; stop_sequence becomes observable and the STOP output phase begins, with no entry into start_sequence, read_sequence, or write_sequence.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset, compare the command-sequence probes against a reference FSM model and verify that stop_sequence is selected on the first clk_en tick with idle asserted.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, scl_i=1, sda_i=1, and cmd=4'b1000 (READ). Hold cmd and ena through the next enabled clock tick while idle.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the enabled idle command-acceptance tick, the FSM enters read_sequence; read_sequence becomes observable and SDA is released for the read operation, with no entry into start_sequence, stop_sequence, or write_sequence.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset, compare read_sequence and sda_oen with the reference FSM model and verify read_sequence is selected at command acceptance.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, scl_i=1, sda_i=1, din=1, and cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE). Hold cmd, din, and ena through the next enabled clock tick while idle.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the enabled idle command-acceptance tick, the FSM enters write_sequence; write_sequence becomes observable and the WRITE phase drives or releases SDA according to din, with no entry into start_sequence, stop_sequence, or read_sequence.
elements.check_method: At each posedge, compare write_sequence and sda_oen with a reference FSM model using din=1, and verify write_sequence is the selected active sequence immediately after the clk_en acceptance tick.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, scl_i=1, sda_i=1, and cmd=4'b0011, an unsupported encoding. Hold cmd and ena for multiple enabled clock ticks while idle.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: the FSM remains idle for every enabled tick, none of start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, or write_sequence becomes active, and cmd_ack remains low.
elements.check_method: Monitor idle and all four command-sequence probes after every posedge for the test interval; compare with a reference decoder and assert that idle stays high, all sequence probes stay low, and no cmd_ack pulse occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1, clk_cnt at a value producing observable clk_en ticks, and hold both external I2C lines high. Issue cmd=START while idle and retain inputs until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the START sequence, scl_oen and sda_oen first remain released, then sda_oen drives SDA low while scl_oen remains released with SCL high, followed by scl_oen driving SCL low. sda_chk remains low throughout the START sequence. cmd_ack is asserted once at completion.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate command-phase scoreboard triggered by clk_en and account for the one-clock registered output latency. Compare scl_oen, sda_oen, and sda_chk against the START phase expectations and verify exactly one cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After establishing a busy transaction, keep ena=1 and both external lines high. Issue cmd=STOP while idle and retain inputs until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the STOP sequence, sda_oen drives SDA low first, scl_oen then releases SCL high, and sda_oen subsequently releases SDA while SCL is high. sda_chk remains low throughout the STOP sequence. cmd_ack is asserted once at completion.
elements.check_method: Monitor the registered output enables after each posedge and match their ordered transitions to the STOP reference sequence, allowing clock-stretching wait if SCL is externally held low. Check that sda_chk is never asserted and that one cmd_ack pulse occurs.

elements.stimulus: Keep ena=1 and issue cmd=READ while idle. Provide the external slave response by driving SDA low for one run and high for a second run, release SCL normally, and retain inputs until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during READ, sda_oen remains released so the slave can drive SDA, scl_oen releases SCL for the read high phase, then drives SCL low after the read window. sda_chk remains low for the entire READ sequence. cmd_ack is asserted once after the low phase.
elements.check_method: Use a READ phase scoreboard synchronized to clk_en and filtered SCL transitions. Compare every registered scl_oen and sda_oen phase, verify sda_chk=0 in all READ phases, and check completion with a single cmd_ack for both SDA response values.

elements.stimulus: Run two enabled WRITE commands with normal SCL: one with din=0 and one with din=1. Keep the external SDA line low for din=0 and high for din=1 during the released high phase, and retain each command until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: for din=0, sda_oen drives SDA low; for din=1, sda_oen releases SDA. In both cases scl_oen releases SCL for the high phase and then drives SCL low. sda_chk is asserted only during the stable released-SDA high phase of WRITE and is low before and after that phase. Each command completes with one cmd_ack and no arbitration loss under matching bus responses.
elements.check_method: Compare the registered output-enable waveforms and sda_chk against a WRITE phase reference model for both din values, sampling after each posedge and aligning transitions to clk_en. Check that sda_chk assertion is confined to the WRITE high phase and that cmd_ack is one clock wide.

elements.stimulus: Issue a valid WRITE with din=1, then observe the same command at three points: before the released SCL high phase, during that high phase, and after SCL is pulled low. Separately issue START, STOP, and READ commands and observe their non-WRITE phases.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: outside the required WRITE stable-high arbitration phase, sda_chk must remain deasserted; it must not be asserted during WRITE setup, WRITE SCL-low completion, or any START, STOP, or READ phase. scl_oen and sda_oen must show the corresponding setup or completion levels rather than the WRITE high-phase pair. Any assertion of sda_chk in these phases, or an output-enable transition early or late relative to the phase, is a failure of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: Run a negative phase-coverage monitor that samples sda_chk and both output enables on every clk_en phase boundary. Assert sda_chk=0 for all non-checking phases and compare the enables to the command-specific reference model, including the registered one-cycle observation latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a supported START command (cmd=0001) with scl_i and sda_i released high. Drive the bus and clock until the START sequence reaches its terminal timing phase and completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: after the terminal phase, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack is high for exactly one clock cycle; cmd_ack is low on the preceding and following clocks, and the final command-phase scl_oen/sda_oen values are followed by the released idle output state.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to identify the terminal phase and sample registered outputs after each posedge. Assert idle=1 and cmd_ack=1 on the completion clock, assert cmd_ack=0 on the immediately preceding and following clocks, and verify scl_oen and sda_oen transition from the terminal phase to the released idle state.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a supported WRITE command (cmd=0100) with din=1. During the released-high WRITE phase, externally hold SDA low so arbitration is lost before the command reaches its terminal timing phase.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of shows: because the command does not complete at its terminal phase, cmd_ack does not produce a one-clock completion pulse and the completion-specific return-to-idle behavior is not observed; the command aborts on arbitration loss, al asserts, and both output enables are released.
elements.check_method: Monitor write_sequence, sda_chk, ssda, al, idle, cmd_ack, scl_oen, and sda_oen at settled posedge samples. Confirm arbitration loss occurs before the normal terminal phase, al becomes asserted, cmd_ack remains low throughout the aborted command, and no completion pulse is generated; verify both output enables are released after the abort.

elements.stimulus: Perform requirements-to-testplan traceability review for item 11; apply no DUT stimulus on behalf of this item.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, present cmd=4'b0001 (START) on a posedge, then observe each enabled clock through command completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during START, sda_oen is initially 1 and scl_oen is 1, then sda_oen becomes 0 while scl_oen remains 1, creating SDA low while SCL is released high; subsequently scl_oen becomes 0, and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock at the terminal START phase.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, use a temporal scoreboard to verify the ordered phases sda_oen=1,scl_oen=1 -> sda_oen=0,scl_oen=1 -> scl_oen=0, followed by a one-clock cmd_ack pulse; reject any SDA-low phase without SCL released high or any missing/extra acknowledgement.

elements.stimulus: After reset with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, hold ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, present cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) while the FSM is idle for multiple enabled clocks, without issuing a START command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: the START sequence is not entered; sda_oen and scl_oen remain 1 in the ordinary released idle state, no SDA-low-while-SCL-high START phase occurs, and cmd_ack remains 0.
