elements.check_method: Monitor the registered output traces and idle probe over the observation window; assert that no transition to sda_oen=0 or scl_oen=0 occurs and that cmd_ack never pulses, distinguishing the absence of the REQ-0087 START behavior from the ordered sequence in TP-0000.

elements.stimulus: Run the requirements-to-testplan traceability check for the source text identified as item 12; do not drive any DUT input because the item is only a numbered-list marker.
elements.expected_response: No DUT behavior, output, timing, or state transition is required or expected for REQ-0088.
elements.check_method: Review the traceability report and confirm REQ-0088@1 is covered by this vacuous element and that the element imposes no DUT assertion beyond the absence of a stated requirement.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, hold scl_i and sda_i high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, then issue cmd=0010 (STOP) while the controller is idle. Keep ena high and allow the command to complete.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0089: during the STOP sequence, sda_oen is low first while scl_oen remains low or is otherwise not yet released, then scl_oen becomes high to release SCL, and finally sda_oen becomes high while scl_oen remains high. The observed output-enable ordering is SDA driven low, SCL released high, then SDA released high, forming a valid STOP condition; cmd_ack is asserted for one clock at completion.
elements.check_method: Sample registered scl_oen and sda_oen after each posedge and use a temporal scoreboard to require the ordered phases sda_oen=0, then scl_oen=1, then sda_oen=1 with scl_oen still 1. Verify the final release phase and one-clock cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, hold scl_i and sda_i high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, and leave cmd=0000 (NOP) while the controller is idle for several enabled timing ticks. Do not issue a STOP command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for REQ-0089: no STOP sequence occurs. sda_oen does not show the required driven-low then released-high transition, scl_oen does not undergo the STOP-specific release ordering, both output enables remain released at their ordinary idle values (scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1), and cmd_ack remains low.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen and sda_oen over the complete observation window and assert that the STOP ordering never appears: no sampled sda_oen=0 phase followed by scl_oen=1 and a final sda_oen=1 phase. Also check cmd_ack remains deasserted.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=0010 (STOP) while idle. Provide a released-high bus and allow the STOP sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL high, then release SDA high while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the filtered SDA rising transition while filtered SCL is high asserts sto_condition, and cmd_ack asserts high for exactly one clock in the STOP command completion phase after the STOP condition is generated.
elements.check_method: Monitor sda_oen and scl_oen for the required STOP ordering, correlate sto_condition with the filtered STOP transition, and assert that cmd_ack has one rising-clock-wide pulse after sto_condition without any additional cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=0010 (STOP) while idle. During the STOP sequence, externally hold SCL low after the controller releases SCL, preventing filtered SCL from becoming high and preventing SDA from rising while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: no filtered STOP condition is generated, and cmd_ack does not assert during the STOP command completion window while the STOP condition is absent.
elements.check_method: Verify filtered SCL remains low, sto_condition never asserts, and use an assertion over the entire stalled STOP interval that cmd_ack remains low; release SCL afterward and separately confirm that any later ack is only associated with a subsequently generated STOP condition.

elements.stimulus: Inspect the controlled specification artifact and select the version containing numbered item 13.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: the specification artifact visibly includes item number 13.
elements.check_method: Parse the specification's numbered-item structure and assert that an item with number 13 is present.

elements.stimulus: Create a controlled negative fixture by removing numbered item 13 from an otherwise identical specification artifact.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case of shows: the specification artifact does not include item number 13; this absence is detected by the check rather than producing any DUT output.
elements.check_method: Parse the negative fixture's numbered-item structure and assert that no item with number 13 is present.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, rst low, ena high, and a released-high bus, issue cmd=READ (1000) on a clock edge; provide a valid external SCL/data-bit timing sequence and continue until the READ data-bit window is reached, before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the READ data-bit window, sda_oen is high, which is the 'shows' side of the observation: SDA is released so the slave can drive the data bit.
elements.check_method: At every clock in the interval from read_sequence becoming active through the clock before cmd_ack, sample the registered sda_oen after nonblocking updates settle and assert it remains 1.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, rst low, ena high, and a released-high bus, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=0 on a clock edge; provide normal SCL timing and continue through the WRITE data-bit phase.
elements.expected_response: During the contrasting non-READ data-bit phase, sda_oen is low, which is the 'otherwise' side of the observation: SDA is driven low rather than released.
elements.check_method: During the active WRITE data-bit phase before cmd_ack, sample the registered sda_oen after nonblocking updates settle and assert it is 0; separately confirm the phase is not read_sequence.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, choose a nonzero clk_cnt, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, and issue cmd=READ while idle on an enabled clk_en tick. Allow the READ operation to reach its SCL sample window, then continue clocks until the window completes.
elements.expected_response: The READ sequence releases SCL by driving scl_oen high throughout the sample window, then drives SCL low by setting scl_oen low at the transition completing the window. This is the holding side of the observed_via shows condition.
elements.check_method: At settled posedge samples, use the read_sequence/read-related timing reference model to identify the sample-window interval; assert scl_oen==1 for the full interval and detect a subsequent scl_oen transition to 0 without reset or command abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=READ with ena=1, but assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the controller reaches the READ SCL sample window; release nReset and observe the reset state without allowing the aborted operation to continue.
elements.expected_response: Because the READ operation is aborted before its sample window, scl_oen does not remain high for a READ sample window followed by becoming low. It returns to the reset-released state instead. This is the contrasting, otherwise side of the observed_via shows condition.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify that the READ sample-window state was never reached; verify asynchronously that reset sets scl_oen high and that no qualifying high-window-then-low sequence occurs before or after the abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue a READ command while the external bus is released high, drive sda_i so that the synchronized and majority-filtered SDA value is 1 before the READ sampling window, and allow the READ sequence to release SCL and produce a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0094: when filtered_scl_rising occurs, dout updates on the processing clock to the current filtered SDA value, 1.
elements.check_method: At every filtered_scl_rising probe event during the READ sequence, sample ssda and compare it with dout after the corresponding posedge update; require dout to equal ssda for the event.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish dout at a known value through a prior READ sample, then issue another READ while externally holding filtered SCL low so no filtered SCL rising edge occurs. Change sda_i from 0 to 1 and allow synchronization and filtering to complete without allowing filtered SCL to rise.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for REQ-0094: because no filtered SCL rising-edge event occurs, dout does not capture the changed filtered SDA value and remains at its prior value.
elements.check_method: Monitor filtered_scl_rising and ssda; whenever ssda changes while filtered_scl_rising is absent, compare dout before and after the update window and require no dout update attributable to that SDA change. Fail if dout changes without a filtered SCL rising edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=READ (4'b1000), and issue the command on a clk_en-enabled clock. Model the external slave as releasing or driving SDA with a valid read bit, allow the released SCL high phase and any required clock stretching to complete, then allow the READ FSM to pull SCL low and reach its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: The READ command completes with cmd_ack asserted for exactly one clock at the terminal phase after the READ command was accepted. No additional cmd_ack pulse is generated for that command.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of clk_en, filtering, clock stretching, and READ phase progression to identify the terminal phase; compare the registered cmd_ack waveform against a single-cycle high pulse at that phase and verify it is low on all other cycles.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) on an enabled clock. Confirm the READ sequence is active, then assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the READ reaches its terminal phase; release nReset and continue clocking without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding side of the observed behavior: the reset-aborted READ does not produce a terminal cmd_ack completion pulse. Reset returns the controller to idle with cmd_ack low.
elements.check_method: Monitor the READ-active indication and asynchronous reset response, then compare cmd_ack against the reference model: it must remain low during and after the aborted operation, except that a pulse already produced before reset would be outside this stimulus window; verify no spurious post-reset pulse occurs.

elements.stimulus: Apply no requirement-specific stimulus; review List item 14 as a scaffolding item with no hardware precondition or prescribed DUT behavior.
elements.expected_response: No hardware output response is required by REQ-0096; the DUT is not constrained by this requirement.
elements.check_method: Manual requirements-to-testplan review confirms the requirement text and normalized expectation specify no observable hardware behavior and that this element introduces no additional DUT assertion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=4, keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, set din=0, issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100) while idle, and provide enabled clocks until the WRITE command completes.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the observed shows: during the WRITE SDA-setting and SCL-high phases, sda_oen=0 because din=0; scl_oen=1 during the SCL-high phase and then becomes 0 for the subsequent SCL-low phase; sda_chk=1 during the stable SCL-high phase.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model to identify WRITE phase entry and completion, then assert sampled-after-posedge temporal checks that sda_oen matches 0 before and during SCL high, scl_oen has the sequence 1 then 0, and sda_chk is asserted only in the stable SCL-high arbitration phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=4, keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, set din=1, issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100) while idle, and provide enabled clocks until the WRITE command completes.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the observed shows: during the WRITE SDA-setting and SCL-high phases, sda_oen=1 because din=1; scl_oen=1 during the SCL-high phase and then becomes 0 for the subsequent SCL-low phase; sda_chk=1 during the stable SCL-high phase, with no arbitration loss because the observed SDA remains high.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model to identify WRITE phase entry and completion, then compare sampled-after-posedge traces for sda_oen=1 before and during SCL high, the required scl_oen 1-to-0 transition, and sda_chk asserted during the stable SCL-high phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the controller idle, set ena=1, clk_cnt=4, keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, set din=0, issue cmd=NOP (4'b0000), and provide enabled clocks for at least the duration of a complete WRITE sequence.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case of the observed shows: because no WRITE command is activated, the controller does not produce the WRITE sequence—sda_chk remains deasserted, and there is no WRITE-specific scl_oen phase of released high followed by pulled low or SDA-setting phase attributable to din. The FSM remains idle and no command acknowledgement is generated.
elements.check_method: Monitor the idle probe and registered outputs after each posedge; assert that no WRITE-sequence interval is entered, sda_chk never asserts, and no scl_oen 1-to-0 transition occurs in the command-sequence window. Confirm the result against the reference model for NOP handling.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high I2C bus, drive cmd=WRITE (0100) and din=0 or 1, and hold the command until the controller accepts it on an enabled clk_en tick. Allow the WRITE sequence to release SCL for its high phase and then pull SCL low without injecting arbitration loss or reset.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after the terminal WRITE phase has pulled SCL low, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock to indicate that the WRITE command sequence has ended; it then deasserts while the FSM returns to idle.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked assertion that a recognized WRITE sequence reaching its terminal SCL-low phase produces cmd_ack=1 on the next registered observation, that cmd_ack remains high for one clock only, and that no duplicate pulse occurs before the next command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1. During the released-SDA, released-SCL arbitration-checking high phase, externally hold SDA low so the filtered SDA is low, causing arbitration loss before the sequence reaches its terminal SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: because the WRITE sequence is aborted before its terminal phase, cmd_ack remains low; the WRITE has no command-complete indication, and both output enables are released after arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Monitor the filtered SDA/arbitration-check phase and assert that al becomes set, the FSM leaves the active WRITE sequence without reaching its normal terminal completion, and cmd_ack never asserts from that aborted command.

elements.stimulus: Apply any legal clocked stimulus, including reset, enable, commands, and bus inputs, without assigning a requirement-specific scenario.
elements.expected_response: No output behavior is required or asserted for this requirement.
elements.check_method: Record the scenario as a coverage-only bin and perform no functional comparison or assertion beyond test execution validity.

elements.stimulus: First deassert nReset and run the controller until it is not in its initial reset state, then assert nReset low between two rising edges of clk and hold it low for several clock cycles. Keep ena high and provide a released-high bus.
elements.expected_response: During the asynchronous reset window, the FSM is idle; scl_oen and sda_oen are high, releasing SCL and SDA; cmd_ack, al, and busy are low; filter_cnt is reset; fscl and fsda are initialized high; and sscl and ssda are high. These are the required-high/low sides of the observed_via shows clauses for REQ-0100.
elements.check_method: Use an asynchronous assertion monitor sampling outputs and licensed probes immediately after the nReset transition, without waiting for clk. Compare scl_oen, sda_oen, cmd_ack, al, busy, idle, filter_cnt, fscl, fsda, sscl, and ssda against the reset reference model, and verify the values remain correct across subsequent posedges while nReset remains low.

elements.stimulus: Release nReset high, keep rst low and ena high, set clk_cnt to 0, ensure the bus is released and high, then issue a START command and hold cmd at NOP after acceptance.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-reset case: once the START sequence is active, sda_oen is driven low during the SDA-low phase rather than remaining high, and the controller is no longer required to have the reset-side values of idle, cmd_ack, al, and busy. The observed port therefore demonstrates the 'otherwise' side of REQ-0100's shows clause: scl_oen/sda_oen are not required to be high outside the asynchronous reset window.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked monitor after each posedge, with clk_cnt=0 modeled as an enabled tick every clock. Confirm the START command is accepted, observe start_sequence or the corresponding output phase, and assert that sda_oen becomes low during the START SDA-low phase; also verify the controller is not continuously held in the reset observation tuple.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset high, ena high, and clk_cnt at 0. Issue a valid START command with scl_i and sda_i released high, and wait until the controller is active or the START sequence is visible. Assert rst high before a rising edge of clk and keep it high through that edge.
elements.expected_response: At the rising edge while rst=1, the synchronous reset behavior holds: idle is asserted, scl_oen and sda_oen become high to release both lines, cmd_ack, al, and busy are low, and the filtered SCL and SDA probes sscl and ssda are high. This is the rst-asserted side of the observed reset behavior.
elements.check_method: At the reset sampling edge, compare registered outputs and idle against reset-reference-model values after nonblocking assignments settle; assert scl_oen==1, sda_oen==1, cmd_ack==0, al==0, busy==0, idle==1, sscl==1, and ssda==1.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset high and rst low, set ena high and clk_cnt to 0, initialize scl_i and sda_i released high, and issue a START command while the controller is idle. Do not assert either reset input during the command sequence.
elements.expected_response: With rst=0, the reset condition does not hold and ordinary command behavior occurs: the controller leaves idle and enters the START sequence, retaining the command-driven output phase such as scl_oen high with sda_oen low while SCL is high, rather than forcing all reset values. This is the non-rst-asserted side of the observed reset behavior.
elements.check_method: After the enabled command-acceptance edge, compare idle and the output-enable waveform with the command reference model; require idle==0 and the START phase to be observable, including scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==0, and ensure no synchronous reset event is recorded.

elements.stimulus: Evaluate the specification document for the i2c_master_bit_ctrl module and locate the section titled "Processing Flow:".
elements.expected_response: The specification contains a processing-flow section titled "Processing Flow:" describing the module's processing flow.
elements.check_method: Static document check: search the specification source for the exact heading "Processing Flow:" and confirm that the section contains processing-flow content.

elements.stimulus: With the controller idle, assert nReset low between clock edges and hold it long enough to observe asynchronous effects; separately deassert nReset, assert rst high across a rising edge, then release rst.
elements.expected_response: Holding-case of REQ-0103: reset and initialization start processing and initialize scl_oen to 1, leaving SCL released. The same released value is present asynchronously for nReset and after the next rising edge for rst.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen immediately after asynchronous nReset assertion and after the first rising edge with rst asserted; compare against 1 and verify no transient 0 or command-driven activity.

elements.stimulus: Release both resets, set ena high and a nonzero clk_cnt, then issue a valid START command on a clk_en-enabled idle cycle while the external SCL and SDA lines are high; allow the START sequence to reach its active phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-reset case of REQ-0103: during the active START command phase that drives SCL low, scl_oen becomes 0 rather than retaining the reset-initialized high value.
elements.check_method: Use the start_sequence/fsm_active probes to identify the active command phase, then sample registered scl_oen after each posedge and compare the active-phase value with the reset baseline of 1; require scl_oen=0 in the SCL-low phase.

elements.stimulus: With nReset=1, rst=0, ena=1, and clk_cnt=0, start a command sequence and create bus activity sufficient to make the controller non-idle; then assert nReset=0 between clock edges and hold it low for at least one clock period.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the reset behavior: immediately when nReset is asserted, the FSM becomes idle, cmd_ack, al, and busy become low, scl_oen and sda_oen become high, sda_chk becomes low, filter_cnt and timing counters are reset or reloaded to their reset values, and sscl and ssda become high. No command progress or completion pulse occurs while reset is asserted.
elements.check_method: Use asynchronous waveform assertions sampled immediately after the nReset transition and again after the next posedge: assert idle=1, cmd_ack=0, al=0, busy=0, scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, sda_chk=0, sscl=1, ssda=1, and the documented reset counter values; verify cmd_ack remains low for successive clocks while nReset=0.

elements.stimulus: With nReset=1, rst=0, ena=1, and clk_cnt=0, begin a command sequence and establish non-idle bus activity; assert rst=1 while nReset remains high, then apply a rising edge of clk and keep rst high for one additional clock.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the synchronous-reset behavior: on the rising edge with rst=1, the FSM returns to idle, cmd_ack, al, and busy are cleared, scl_oen and sda_oen are released high, arbitration checking is disabled, counters are reset or reloaded to their reset values, and sscl and ssda are initialized high. The reset state persists while rst remains asserted.
elements.check_method: At the posedge that samples rst=1, compare registered outputs and probes against the reset reference model: idle=1, cmd_ack=0, al=0, busy=0, scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, sda_chk=0, sscl=1, ssda=1, and reset counter values; verify no reset response occurs before that posedge and no command progress occurs while rst=1.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset=1 and rst=0 throughout. Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a valid START command while the bus is released high, and allow the FSM to reach its SDA-low START phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-reset case: the controller remains non-idle while executing the command, and ordinary command behavior is visible rather than the reset behavior; specifically sda_oen may be driven low during START and idle=0, while cmd_ack is not forced low solely by reset and busy may become high after the filtered START is detected.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked assertion conditioned on nReset=1 and rst=0 during start_sequence: require idle=0 and the specified START output-enable phase, and confirm the reset signature is absent (sda_oen is not required to remain high and the FSM is not idle); correlate busy with sta_condition and check that no reset event occurred.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, deassert it, keep rst low and ena high, then drive scl_i=0 and sda_i=0 for multiple enabled clk rising edges followed by scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 for multiple enabled clk rising edges.
elements.expected_response: After reset synchronization latency, cscl and csda reflect the sampled external values: both become 0 during the low interval and both become 1 during the high interval, without requiring a command.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, compare cscl and csda with a cycle-accurate two-stage synchronizer reference model driven by scl_i and sda_i; require agreement for both all-zero and all-one input cases.

elements.stimulus: After reset deassertion with rst low and ena high, apply a sequence of independent scl_i and sda_i transitions on successive clock intervals, including 00, 01, 10, and 11, and hold each combination long enough to pass through synchronization.
elements.expected_response: cscl and csda continuously track the corresponding scl_i and sda_i samples with the modeled synchronization latency, including independent changes on either input and successive transitions.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate scoreboard for the synchronized bus-sample registers, comparing every settled clock's cscl/csda values against the expected two-stage capture of the current input sequence; flag missed, stale, or cross-coupled samples.

elements.stimulus: After reset deassertion, drive scl_i and sda_i through distinct high/low transitions while ena is high, changing values between successive rising edges of clk and holding each value across at least three rising edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on every rising edge of clk, the two-stage synchronization pipeline captures the current raw scl_i and sda_i values. cscl and csda reflect the corresponding raw values with the expected two-clock synchronization delay, and each sustained input value eventually propagates to its probe.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after nonblocking assignments settle, compare cscl and csda against a reference model containing two serial registers per input. Record coverage for both 0-to-1 and 1-to-0 transitions on scl_i and sda_i.

elements.stimulus: With the synchronized probes stable, toggle scl_i and sda_i shortly after a rising edge of clk, then toggle them again before the next rising edge; repeat with independent transitions on each input while observing cscl and csda between clock edges.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: when the synchronous capture event is absent, asynchronous changes on raw scl_i or sda_i do not immediately change cscl or csda. The probes retain their previous synchronized values until subsequent rising edges capture and propagate the inputs through both synchronization stages.
elements.check_method: Sample cscl and csda during the intervals between posedges and assert they remain unchanged despite raw input toggles. On subsequent posedges, compare propagation against the two-stage reference model and verify no combinational raw-input path exists.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, then deassert it before a rising edge. Drive scl_i=0 and sda_i=0 after reset, and observe cscl and csda across two successive rising edges of clk while keeping the inputs stable.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement: cscl and csda initially retain their reset-high values, then reflect the corresponding low inputs only after the two-stage capture sequence has completed. The controller-visible probes must not use the newly driven raw values before the capture pipeline has propagated them.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, compare cscl/csda against a reference model containing two serial capture stages. Bin the initial retained value and the value after the second capture stage; fail on any immediate one-stage or combinational propagation.

elements.stimulus: With the capture pipeline initialized, change scl_i and sda_i from 0 to 1 immediately before a rising edge, then change them back to 0 immediately after the next rising edge. Continue clocking for at least three rising edges while recording the raw inputs and cscl/csda.
elements.expected_response: Not-holding/direct-use contrast: cscl and csda must not track the raw transitions immediately or in the same capture edge. Any observation equivalent to direct or single-stage use of scl_i/sda_i at cscl/csda is a failure; the probes must instead follow the two-stage delayed sequence, including retaining the prior value while the new sample propagates.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate scoreboard for two-stage capture and compare each cscl/csda sample with both the current raw input and the one- and two-cycle delayed models. Confirm that the two-cycle model matches and that immediate/direct and one-cycle models do not.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it, then set rst=0, ena=1, and clk_cnt=8. Hold scl_i=0 and sda_i=0 long enough for two-stage synchronization and at least three filter sampling updates; then drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 and hold both high long enough for synchronization and at least three further filter sampling updates.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cscl and csda first reflect the captured low bus values and later reflect the captured high values; after the filter pipeline has accumulated the stable high samples, sscl=1 and ssda=1. The filtered outputs change only after the expected synchronization and filter-sampling delay, not immediately on the raw input transition.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage capture, filter sampling interval, three-sample histories, and majority filtering. At every posedge after nonblocking updates settle, compare cscl/csda and sscl/ssda against the model and require the final filtered values to equal the stable captured inputs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, establish scl_i=0 and sda_i=0 until cscl=0, csda=0 and sscl=0, ssda=0. Drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 only long enough for one filter sampling update, then return both inputs to 0 and hold them low for at least three filter sampling updates.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the brief captured high excursion may appear in cscl/csda, but it does not satisfy the filter's stable-sample requirement; sscl and ssda remain 0 throughout the excursion and afterward. Thus the filtered outputs show the no-propagation side of the filtering behavior rather than following the transient captured values.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed cscl/csda and sscl/ssda waveforms with a reference model implementing the synchronizer, filter sampling schedule, three-sample history, and majority result. Assert that no sscl or ssda rising transition occurs for the one-sample pulse, while the outputs remain at 0 after the pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16, keep scl_i and sda_i stable, and provide enabled clock cycles until filter_cnt is reloaded and then expires.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0109: filter_cnt reloads to the sampling interval clk_cnt >> 2 = 4, and filter sampling occurs after the corresponding four-count interval rather than after 16 counts or an unrelated value.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk, compare the filter_cnt probe against a reference counter loaded with unsigned(clk_cnt >> 2), and check the observed reload and expiration interval.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and the filter active, first apply clk_cnt=16 and observe a reload interval of 4, then change clk_cnt to 20 and allow the next filter-counter reload while keeping scl_i and sda_i stable.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for REQ-0109: filter_cnt changes with clk_cnt, from the prior interval of 4 to clk_cnt >> 2 = 5. A design that ignores clk_cnt or uses clk_cnt without the two-bit shift would show no such 4-to-5 change and fails.
elements.check_method: Record filter_cnt reload values and intervals at the probe, and compare them cycle-by-cycle with a reference model computing floor(clk_cnt/4) for each applied prescaler value.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, then drive scl_i and sda_i low continuously. Run posedges until the two-stage synchronized values cscl and csda are low and the filter counter reaches filter_cnt=0 while filter progression is enabled.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when filter_cnt expires, the controller shifts the current synchronized SCL and SDA samples into fscl and fsda on that enabled sampling event. The histories must update in the reference-model shift order, with the newly synchronized low samples entering the histories.
elements.check_method: At each posedge, compare fscl and fsda with a reference model that synchronizes the inputs, tracks the derived filter interval, and shifts cscl and csda only when filter_cnt expires. Require a history update at the modeled expiration event and bin the expiration-to-history-shift observation.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16, then drive scl_i and sda_i low continuously. After a filter sampling event reloads filter_cnt, observe one or more enabled posedges while filter_cnt is nonzero and before its next expiration.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: while filter_cnt is nonzero, the controller must not shift new synchronized samples into fscl or fsda; both histories remain at their prior reference-model values until the next filter-counter expiration.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter-counter model to identify enabled posedges before expiration and compare fscl and fsda after each posedge. Require no history shift on those posedges, then confirm the shift occurs only at the subsequent modeled expiration event.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it, keep rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then drive scl_i=0 and sda_i=0 continuously for enough enabled clocks to pass the two-stage synchronizers and three filter sampling expirations. Continue clocking until filter_cnt expires and fscl and fsda contain three low samples.
elements.expected_response: On the filter-counter expiration that shifts the third low sample, fscl and fsda are updated and sscl=0 and ssda=0, because the majority of each three-sample history is low. This is the holding case of the requirement: filter_cnt expires, histories update, and the filtered outputs are the corresponding majority values.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, use a reference model of the synchronizers, history shifts, and three-sample majority function; on filter_cnt expiration compare sscl to majority(fscl) and ssda to majority(fsda), and specifically require both outputs to be 0 for the final all-low histories.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. First drive scl_i=0 and sda_i=0 until three filter sampling expirations establish all-low histories, then drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 continuously for enough enabled clocks to pass synchronization and three further filter sampling expirations.
elements.expected_response: At the expiration that shifts the third high sample, fscl and fsda become all high and sscl=1 and ssda=1. This is the holding case of the requirement for the opposite data value: the filtered outputs must be high because the majority of each three-sample history is high.
elements.check_method: Track expected fscl and fsda shift registers and calculate each three-bit majority after every filter_cnt expiration. Compare the probe outputs sscl and ssda against those calculated values, requiring both to transition from 0 to 1 only after the modeled history updates.

elements.stimulus: Establish sscl=1 and ssda=1 with clk_cnt=0, then change scl_i and sda_i to 0 while ena remains 1 and clk_cnt is set to a nonzero value. Begin the input change immediately after a filter sampling update and clock for fewer enabled clocks than required for filter_cnt to expire, verifying filter_cnt remains nonzero during the observation window.
elements.expected_response: While filter_cnt has not expired, fscl and fsda are not shifted and sscl and ssda retain their previous majority-derived high values, despite the changed synchronized input samples. This is the contrasting non-holding case of the requirement: without filter-counter expiration and history update, the filtered outputs must not respond to the new samples.
elements.check_method: Use the reference timing model to identify cycles before filter_cnt expiration, compare fscl/fsda with their pre-stimulus values, and assert sscl=1 and ssda=1 throughout that interval; also verify no filtered-output change occurs until a subsequent expiration updates the histories.

elements.stimulus: After asynchronous reset with nReset low then high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4. Keep the external SCL and SDA lines high long enough for the filter histories to contain three high samples. Then hold SCL low and SDA low continuously for at least three filter sampling updates, followed by returning both lines high continuously for at least three filter sampling updates.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: sscl and ssda represent the stable internal filtered bus lines: each changes from high to low only after the sustained low level establishes the majority-filtered value, and changes back to high only after the sustained high level establishes the majority-filtered value. The probes do not follow the raw line immediately.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the synchronizers, filter sampling interval, three-sample histories, and majority function. At every enabled filter update, compare sscl and ssda with the model's filtered SCL and SDA values and verify the expected delayed transitions.

elements.stimulus: After reset, with ena=1 and clk_cnt=4, establish stable high SCL and SDA so sscl=1 and ssda=1. Drive both external lines low for only one filter sampling update, then return them high and keep them high for at least three further filter sampling updates.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: because the low input is only a short glitch and does not establish a majority-filtered bus value, sscl and ssda remain high throughout; the filtered internal signals do not reproduce the transient raw-line values.
elements.check_method: Compare sscl and ssda cycle by cycle against a three-sample-majority reference model, and assert that neither probe changes to zero during the one-sample low glitch or generates a corresponding filtered transition.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, then operate with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 while keeping the external SCL and SDA bus lines stably high for multiple enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: sscl and ssda remain high, and dscl and dsda maintain the delayed filtered values as high on every sampled clock; no delayed-signal transition occurs while the filtered signals are stable.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset and after nonblocking assignments settle, compare dscl and dsda against the reference model's delayed sscl and ssda histories; record a bin for stable-high filtered inputs and assert equality for every cycle.

elements.stimulus: With nReset released, ena=1, and clk_cnt=0, hold both external bus lines high long enough for the filters to settle, then drive SCL and SDA low continuously for at least the synchronizer and three-sample filter latency, and finally return both lines high for the same duration.
elements.expected_response: Transition case: when sscl or ssda changes, dscl and dsda retain the preceding filtered values for the delayed-signal interval rather than immediately mirroring the new sscl and ssda values; on the following delayed update they assume the new filtered values. The same one-sample delayed relationship is observed for the return to high.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronization, majority filtering, and delayed registers. On every filtered transition, assert dscl[n]=sscl[n-1] and dsda[n]=ssda[n-1], and flag any cycle where dscl/dsda instead equal the current filtered values before the modeled delay expires.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, and allow the initialized bus to be filtered high. Then hold scl_i high and drive sda_i low long enough for the synchronizer, filter history, and delayed filtered SDA to update through a filtered high-to-low transition.
elements.expected_response: When the current filtered SDA is low, the delayed filtered SDA is high, and filtered SCL is high, the controller detects the comparison as a START event; busy rises on the corresponding registered update and remains high while the bus remains active. This is the event-detected side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, compare ssda and dsda and require the busy transition only when ssda=0, dsda=1, and sscl=1. Confirm the transition is not caused by raw SDA before the filtered/delayed probe relationship occurs, and check that busy becomes 1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, first create a filtered START by holding scl_i high and driving sda_i low until busy is high. Then hold scl_i high and drive sda_i high long enough for a filtered low-to-high SDA transition and its delayed value to be established.
elements.expected_response: When the current filtered SDA is high, the delayed filtered SDA is low, and filtered SCL is high, the controller detects the comparison as a STOP event; busy falls on the corresponding registered update. This is the contrasting event-detected side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Monitor ssda, dsda, sscl, and busy on settled posedge samples. Require a busy falling transition only at a sample with ssda=1, dsda=0, and sscl=1, after confirming busy was previously high from the START setup.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish busy=0 after reset, then apply either no SDA transition while scl_i remains high or a filtered SDA transition while scl_i is low. Hold each condition long enough for ssda and dsda to become equal and stable.
elements.expected_response: When current and delayed filtered values are equal, or when an SDA transition occurs while filtered SCL is low, no important START/STOP event is detected and busy remains at its previous value. This is the non-event side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter model to identify intervals where ssda=dsda or where ssda differs from dsda while sscl=0. Assert that busy does not change during those intervals, while also checking that no busy pulse or spurious status transition occurs.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish both filtered SCL and filtered SDA high by driving scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 for enough enabled clocks to fill the synchronizer and filter histories, then keep scl_i=1 and drive sda_i=0 long enough for filtered SDA to transition from high to low.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered SDA falling transition occurs while filtered SCL remains high, the controller detects an I2C START condition and asserts sta_condition. This is the asserted side of the requirement's observed behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, compare sta_condition with a reference model of the two-stage synchronizers, three-sample majority filter, delayed filtered SDA, and filtered SCL. Require sta_condition=1 on the modeled filtered SDA high-to-low transition with filtered SCL=1, and record the corresponding sscl=1 and ssda falling transition.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish filtered SCL high and filtered SDA high, then drive scl_i=0 and hold it long enough for filtered SCL to become low; while filtered SCL remains low, drive sda_i=0 long enough for filtered SDA to transition from high to low, then keep both lines stable.
elements.expected_response: The controller does not detect an I2C START condition for the SDA high-to-low transition because filtered SCL is low; sta_condition remains deasserted. This is the non-applicable side of the requirement's observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to identify the filtered SDA falling edge and verify sscl=0 at that edge. Compare the observed sta_condition against the model and require no sta_condition assertion during the transition or while filtered SCL remains low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Drive the external bus released-high on SCL and SDA, then hold scl_i=1 while drive sda_i low long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce sscl=1 and ssda=0. Next release sda_i high and hold both scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 long enough for the filtered SDA value to transition from 0 to 1.
elements.expected_response: Positive side of the specified behavior: when sscl=1 and ssda transitions low-to-high, the controller detects the STOP condition by asserting sto_condition for the corresponding filtered transition.
elements.check_method: Sample sscl, ssda, dsda, and sto_condition after each posedge clk; use a reference model of the synchronizer and three-sample majority filter to identify the filtered SDA rising edge, then compare sto_condition against an assertion that it is high on that detected edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Establish and maintain scl_i=1 long enough for sscl=1, and drive sda_i=0 long enough for ssda=0. Keep sda_i low without any low-to-high transition; additionally apply a high glitch shorter than the filter interval and return sda_i low before the filtered history can change.
elements.expected_response: Negative side of the specified behavior: because filtered SDA does not transition from low to high while filtered SCL is high, the controller must not assert sto_condition.
elements.check_method: Monitor sscl, ssda, dsda, and sto_condition after each posedge clk; verify with the filter reference model that ssda has no rising edge while sscl=1, and compare against a check requiring sto_condition to remain deasserted throughout the steady-low and rejected-glitch intervals.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset, then release it with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and both external I2C lines high. Drive SDA low while SCL remains high long enough for synchronization and the three-sample filter to produce a filtered SDA high-to-low transition and assert sta_condition.
elements.expected_response: The START condition side of the requirement holds: busy is set high at the registered status update immediately following the detected filtered START and remains high until a STOP condition is detected.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset release, compare busy against a reference model of the synchronized/filtered SDA and SCL transitions; require sta_condition=1 and busy to transition from 0 to 1 on the following registered update.

elements.stimulus: First establish busy=1 by generating a filtered START with SDA falling while SCL is high. Then, with ena=1 and SCL still high, drive SDA high long enough for the filter to produce a filtered SDA low-to-high transition and assert sto_condition.
elements.expected_response: The STOP condition side of the requirement holds: busy is cleared low at the registered status update immediately following the detected filtered STOP and remains low until a subsequent START condition.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for filtered START/STOP detection and sample busy after nonblocking updates at each posedge; require sto_condition=1 and busy to transition from 1 to 0 on the following registered update.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a valid READ command with clk_cnt=1. During the READ high phase, allow the DUT to release SCL by observing scl_oen=1, then externally hold SCL low so filtered SCL remains low for several enabled clock periods. Release the external SCL drive high and continue supplying a valid bus response.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the requirement: while scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL remains low, cmd_ack is withheld and the READ command does not complete. After filtered SCL becomes high and the required low-period timing is accommodated, the command proceeds and produces its terminal cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the divider, filtered SCL, slave_wait, FSM phase, and command completion. Assert that no cmd_ack occurs during the filtered-low interval, then compare the observed cmd_ack timing and pulse width against the model after SCL release.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a valid WRITE command with din=1 and clk_cnt=1. During a phase in which the DUT has released SCL, externally force a filtered SCL falling event to model another master synchronizing the shared clock, then release SCL high and allow the bus to continue normally.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the requirement for multi-master clock synchronization: cmd_ack is withheld while the synchronized external low period is being handled, the command does not complete prematurely, and cmd_ack occurs only after the timing counter has been reloaded/accommodated and the WRITE sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.check_method: Monitor filtered SCL edges, scl_sync, cnt_zero, clk_en, FSM activity, and cmd_ack. Compare against a reference model that reloads the low-period timing on the released-SCL falling event and verify no early cmd_ack and exactly one terminal-cycle pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a valid START command with clk_cnt=1 on a bus whose filtered SCL remains high whenever the DUT releases it; do not apply any external SCL stretching or falling-edge synchronization event.
elements.expected_response: This is the otherwise side of the requirement: with filtered SCL high and no external SCL synchronization event, the START sequence completes normally and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock at its normal terminal phase.
elements.check_method: Use the divider/FSM reference model to predict the normal START terminal phase. Check that cmd_ack is absent before that phase, asserted for one clock only at the predicted completion, and that no stretch or synchronization delay is observed.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a supported command that reaches an SCL-high phase, such as READ (cmd=1000). Model the bus open-drain behavior so that when the DUT releases SCL (scl_oen=1), an external participant holds scl_i low long enough for the filtered SCL probe sscl to remain 0 across the enabled timing updates.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the observed behavior: while scl_oen=1 and sscl=0 during the enabled command sequence, the DUT asserts slave_wait=1, holds the command's high-phase progression, and does not advance until either SCL is driven low by the controller or sscl becomes 1.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge of clk, compare the slave_wait probe against the predicate ena && scl_oen && !sscl during the active command sequence; verify slave_wait is asserted while the predicate holds and that the FSM/output phase does not progress until the predicate clears.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue the same supported command sequence, but allow the external bus to remain high so that when the DUT releases SCL (scl_oen=1), the synchronized and filtered SCL probe sscl reaches 1.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case of the observed behavior: with scl_oen=1 and sscl=1, the DUT does not assert slave_wait (slave_wait=0) and the command advances through the released-high phase on the next permitted clk_en timing event.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge of clk during the released-high phase, assert that sscl=1 implies slave_wait=0 and use the reference timing model to verify that FSM/output progression occurs at the next clk_en event rather than being held for clock stretching.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a READ command with the bus initially high, and externally hold SCL low while the controller releases it (scl_oen=1); keep the external SCL low long enough for sscl to remain 0.
elements.expected_response: The controller reaches the SCL-release phase of the READ sequence, and slave_wait asserts while scl_oen=1 and sscl=0. This is the holding case: the asserted slave_wait condition indicates that a slave or another bus participant is holding SCL low.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare scl_oen, sscl, and slave_wait against a reference model of the filtered SCL and slave-wait condition; require slave_wait=1 during the released-SCL/filtered-low interval and require no command-phase advancement until filtered SCL becomes high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a READ command with the bus high, and allow the externally released SCL line to remain high so that the filtered SCL reaches sscl=1 during the controller's SCL-release phase.
elements.expected_response: The controller reaches the SCL-release phase with scl_oen=1, but slave_wait does not assert once sscl is high. This is the contrasting non-holding case: the absence of an asserted slave_wait condition indicates that no participant is holding SCL low.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare scl_oen, sscl, and slave_wait with the reference model; require slave_wait=0 when scl_oen=1 and sscl=1, and verify the READ sequence can proceed according to the enabled timing.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=1, and issue a supported WRITE command while the bus is initially high. When the WRITE sequence releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1), externally hold SCL low long enough for filtered SCL to become low and slave_wait to assert; maintain the low condition for several enabled clocks, then release SCL and allow it to filter high.
elements.expected_response: While slave_wait is active, the timing counter remains paused, clk_en does not advance the command timing, scl_oen remains 1 in the released-SCL phase, and cmd_ack does not pulse. After filtered SCL becomes high, the FSM resumes, progresses to the next phase, and eventually produces the normal one-clock cmd_ack. This is the holding-case side of the specified port behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate divider/FSM reference model and sample after each posedge. Correlate the slave_wait interval with unchanged timing/FSM phase, stable scl_oen=1, and absence of cmd_ack; then verify progress and exactly one cmd_ack after filtered SCL is high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=1, and issue the same supported WRITE command with the external bus held high. When the WRITE sequence releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1), keep SCL high so filtered SCL remains high and slave_wait does not assert.
elements.expected_response: Because slave_wait is inactive and the required filtered-SCL condition is already satisfied, the timing counter continues to generate timing ticks, the FSM advances from the released-SCL phase, scl_oen changes to the subsequent commanded phase, and the command reaches its terminal phase with a one-clock cmd_ack without the stretching delay. This is the non-holding-case side of the specified port behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed scl_oen phase transition and cmd_ack timing against the same reference model with no slave-wait interval. Confirm that progress occurs on the next permitted timing tick and that exactly one cmd_ack is generated without any externally imposed SCL-low pause.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4. Issue a valid WRITE command with din=0. During the WRITE phase when scl_oen=1 and the synchronized/filtered SCL is high, hold scl_i high for several clocks, then drive scl_i low and keep it low long enough for synchronization and filtering to recognize the falling edge.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered external SCL falling edge is detected while scl_oen remains 1, scl_sync asserts. The timing counter reloads from clk_cnt, and the controller's subsequent low-period timing is synchronized to the shared bus clock rather than continuing from the pre-edge counter phase. This is the asserted side of the SCL-fall distinction.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage SCL synchronizer, filter history, filtered falling-edge detection, counter reload, and clk_en generation. At the cycle where filtered_scl_falling becomes true with scl_oen=1, compare the scl_sync probe and cnt/filter timing probes against the model, and verify the next local low-period tick sequence starts from the reload value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4. Issue the same valid WRITE command with din=0. During the WRITE phase when scl_oen=1 and SCL is high, keep scl_i high continuously for the entire released-SCL phase; do not apply an external SCL falling edge.
elements.expected_response: While scl_oen=1 and scl_i remains high, scl_sync stays deasserted and the timing counter is not reloaded due to external SCL synchronization; local timing proceeds according to the ordinary clk_cnt-derived schedule. This is the non-asserted contrast side of the SCL-fall distinction.
elements.check_method: Use the same reference timing model and compare scl_sync, cnt_zero, clk_en, and counter/reload behavior on every enabled clock throughout the released-high phase. Confirm no filtered SCL falling event, synchronization assertion, or externally-triggered counter reload occurs.

elements.stimulus: Hold rst low only for reset initialization, then deassert resets, set ena=1, provide a released-high non-stretching bus, set din=1, and issue a WRITE command with clk_cnt=1. Repeat the WRITE with the same conditions and clk_cnt=16. Record the posedges at WRITE stable-high entry, filtered SCL high/released phase, and the subsequent SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen changes from the WRITE stable-high/released phase to the subsequent SCL-low phase only on counter-generated clk_en timing, and the measured interval for clk_cnt=16 is consistently longer than for clk_cnt=1 according to the cnt reload/expiration behavior; no arbitration loss or stretch extends the interval.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of cnt reload, decrement, expiration, and clk_en generation for each clk_cnt. At settled posedge observations, compare the measured scl_oen phase-boundary cycles and internal clk_en/cnt_zero probes against the model, and assert that changing clk_cnt changes the interval in the modeled direction.

elements.stimulus: Run enabled, non-stretched WRITE commands while sweeping clk_cnt across 1, 4, 16, and 65535, including changing clk_cnt between otherwise identical transactions. Observe scl_oen phase boundaries from WRITE stable-high entry through the terminal SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: scl_oen must not exhibit a fixed or clk_cnt-independent phase interval, nor change at intervals unrelated to the internal counter; each transaction's phase-boundary interval must follow the corresponding clk_cnt-derived cnt/clk_en schedule. Any interval that remains unchanged across the sweep or changes independently of clk_cnt fails the requirement.
elements.check_method: Bucket measured scl_oen transition intervals by clk_cnt and compare them with the reference counter model. Flag a failure if transitions occur without the expected clk_en/cnt_zero event or if statistically identical intervals persist for materially different clk_cnt values under identical bus conditions.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, set clk_cnt=3, issue a START command, and keep all bus inputs stable with no stretching or synchronization event. Record scl_oen on every posedge clk through the complete START sequence.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of REQ-0124: scl_oen changes through the START sequence only at phase boundaries predicted by a reference counter that loads clk_cnt=3 and decrements once per rising edge of clk until expiry; the SDA-low-while-SCL-high phase, subsequent SCL-low phase, and terminal command timing occur at those calculated boundaries.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the counter load, one-decrement-per-posedge behavior, clk_en generation, and START FSM phases. Compare each sampled scl_oen transition and terminal phase against the model, allowing no unmodeled early or late transition.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the identical reset, stable-bus, ena=1 START-command scenario with clk_cnt=7 instead of clk_cnt=3. Record scl_oen on every posedge clk and compare the resulting phase-transition trace with TP-0000.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of REQ-0124: the scl_oen phase transitions and command terminal boundary must differ from the clk_cnt=3 trace by the additional counter intervals predicted by loading 7 and decrementing once per rising edge. An invariant or fixed-latency scl_oen trace, or transitions earlier than the clk_cnt=7 reference prediction, is the otherwise side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Run the same cycle-accurate counter/FSM reference model for clk_cnt=7, compare every scl_oen transition and completion cycle against that prediction, and perform a differential comparison against the clk_cnt=3 run to ensure the prescale-dependent interval is observable.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, then provide enabled rising-edge clock cycles until the reference divider reaches zero.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the clock cycle when the internal counter expires (cnt_zero=1), the module asserts clk_en=1 for the timing-enable tick used by the command FSM.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking updates settle, compare clk_en with a reference 16-bit divider model loaded from clk_cnt and decremented while ena=1; require clk_en=1 on the model's expiration cycle.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, then observe one or more enabled rising-edge clock cycles before the reference divider reaches zero.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: while the counter has not expired (cnt_zero=0), the module does not assert clk_en; clk_en remains 0 until the expiration cycle.
elements.check_method: Use the same reference divider model to identify cycles with a nonzero counter and compare the sampled clk_en output after each posedge; require clk_en=0 on every non-expiration cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set clk_cnt to 3, keep ena high, hold scl_i and sda_i high, and issue cmd=START while idle. After the START sequence is accepted and an active phase is reached, sample a clock edge for which clk_en=0 while the current and next START phases would require different scl_oen values.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed_via shows: scl_oen remains at its current command-phase value on the clk_en=0 edge; the active FSM phase does not advance even though the START sequence is in progress.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, sample clk_en, the active-sequence probe, and scl_oen after registered updates settle. At a qualifying active edge with clk_en=0, compare scl_oen against its value before the edge and require no change; maintain a reference FSM phase model to confirm the phase is held.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set clk_cnt to 3, keep ena high, hold scl_i and sda_i high, and issue cmd=START while idle. Wait until the START sequence reaches the phase boundary where SDA has been pulled low with SCL released, then continue clocking until the next qualifying edge with clk_en=1.
elements.expected_response: Changing case of the observed_via shows: scl_oen changes to the next START command-phase value on the clk_en=1 edge, specifically transitioning from released SCL (scl_oen=1) to driven-low SCL (scl_oen=0); the phase advance occurs only on that timing-enable edge.
elements.check_method: Use the reference divider/FSM model to identify the active phase boundary and expected next scl_oen value. Sample scl_oen after each posedge and require the expected transition on the edge where clk_en=1, while checking that no earlier edge caused the transition.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to 1, provide a released-high bus, assert ena high, issue a supported START command, and after the command has been accepted but before its terminal phase drive ena low and hold it low for several clk rising edges.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding-case side of the observed behavior: cmd_ack remains low and the current command output-enable phase remains unchanged for the entire ena=0 interval; timing-enable activity does not advance the command, consistent with the timing counter being reloaded. When ena is reasserted high, the command resumes and eventually produces exactly one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: At each posedge while ena=0, compare cmd_ack and scl_oen/sda_oen with their values at the first disabled cycle and assert that they do not progress toward the next command phase. Observe the clk_en probe remains inactive during the disabled interval, then verify phase progression and a single-cycle cmd_ack after ena returns high.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same setup with clk_cnt set to 1 and a released-high bus, assert ena high, issue the same supported START command, and keep ena high continuously through command completion.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting ordinary-behavior side: the FSM advances through the command sequence, the output-enable phases change as required, and cmd_ack pulses for exactly one clock when the sequence completes.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-by-cycle scoreboard on scl_oen, sda_oen, the start_sequence/idle probes, and clk_en to confirm enabled timing progression; verify that cmd_ack transitions from low to high for one clock and then returns low without an ena-induced pause.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=1, and drive a released-high bus with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. Issue cmd=WRITE and hold the command inputs stable until the command completes.
elements.expected_response: The controller enters and executes the WRITE sequence. During the stable high phase of the WRITE bit, while SDA is released for arbitration, sda_chk is asserted; it is not required outside that WRITE checking phase. The command completes with cmd_ack=1 and no arbitration loss when the observed SDA remains high.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model or waveform assertion to identify the WRITE stable-high phase, then compare sda_chk against 1 in that phase and against the expected deasserted value in other WRITE phases.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and drive a released-high bus. Issue cmd=READ and hold the command inputs stable until the command completes; provide a stable external SDA value and allow the read operation to proceed.
elements.expected_response: The controller executes the READ sequence, but sda_chk remains deasserted throughout the operation because arbitration checking is not performed for this non-WRITE command. The READ completes normally with cmd_ack=1.
elements.check_method: Monitor the read_sequence and command interval using the reference model, and assert that sda_chk is never 1 from READ command acceptance through cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=WRITE (0100), din=1, and keep the externally resolved SDA and SCL lines high. Drive clocks until the WRITE sequence reaches its stable high phase with SCL released.
elements.expected_response: When write_sequence is active in the stable high phase of the WRITE bit, sda_chk is asserted high. This is the side of shows where the observed port indicates that the requirement holds.
elements.check_method: Use the write-sequence reference model to identify the stable high phase and compare the sampled sda_chk probe after each posedge; require sda_chk=1 in that phase.

elements.stimulus: Using the same enabled WRITE transaction with clk_cnt=0 and din=1, observe the WRITE setup/low phase before SCL is released high and the subsequent phase after SCL is pulled low again.
elements.expected_response: While write_sequence is active but the WRITE bit is not in its stable high phase, sda_chk remains low. This is the side of shows where the observed port indicates that the requirement does not hold.
elements.check_method: Track the WRITE phase with the reference FSM model and compare sda_chk after each posedge; require sda_chk=0 in every sampled non-stable-high WRITE phase.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset until al is low, then deassert reset. Set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=1, and issue the WRITE command cmd=0100 while the bus is initially high. Follow the command sequence until write_sequence=1, sda_chk=1, and sda_oen=1; while this stable high phase is active, externally pull SDA low so filtered SDA ssda becomes 0 and hold it until sda_chk clears.
elements.expected_response: The arbitration-loss response side of the observation applies: al asserts high on the clock processing the condition where SDA is released high, sda_chk=1, and filtered SDA ssda=0. The WRITE operation is aborted and no command-complete pulse is generated for the aborted operation.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, assert the activation probes write_sequence, sda_chk, and sda_oen, confirm ssda=0 from the filter model, and compare al against a reference model requiring a low-to-high transition that remains sticky until reset. Confirm no cmd_ack pulse follows the abort.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset until al is low, then deassert reset. Set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=1, and issue the WRITE command cmd=0100 while the bus remains high. Follow the command sequence until write_sequence=1, sda_chk=1, and sda_oen=1; keep the externally observed SDA high so filtered SDA ssda remains 1 throughout the stable high phase, then allow the WRITE sequence to complete.
elements.expected_response: The otherwise side of the observation applies: because the released SDA is not observed low by the filtered input, al does not newly assert and remains low during this operation.
elements.check_method: After reset, monitor every settled posedge during the stable high WRITE phase, verify write_sequence=1, sda_chk=1, sda_oen=1, and ssda=1, and compare al with a reference model that requires it to remain 0; separately check that no al transition occurs before command completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al low, set ena=1 and issue a READ command from idle. Wait until the READ sequence is active, SCL is released high, and SDA is released. Drive the external bus so filtered SDA transitions from low to high while filtered SCL remains high, sustaining the levels long enough to produce sto_condition=1. Do not assert either reset input afterward.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered STOP-detection edge while the non-STOP command is active, al asserts; this is the holding side of the observed behavior. The active READ command aborts, both output enables are released, and no cmd_ack is generated for the aborted command. al remains asserted on subsequent clocks until reset.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered STOP probe and fsm_active/read_sequence probes to identify the qualifying edge, then sample al after the corresponding posedge and compare against a reference model. Assert that al changes from 0 to 1 on that edge, remains 1, and that no command-complete pulse occurs after the abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al low, set ena=1 and issue a STOP command from idle. Allow the STOP sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL high, and release SDA while filtered SCL is high so the controller's requested STOP produces sto_condition=1. Keep both reset inputs inactive.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered STOP condition occurs for the requested STOP command, al does not newly assert; this is the contrasting side of the observed behavior. The STOP sequence completes normally and produces exactly one cmd_ack pulse, while al remains 0.
elements.check_method: Correlate stop_sequence, sto_condition, cmd_ack, and al at settled posedge observations and compare with a reference model. Check that the STOP-detection edge occurs during the requested STOP sequence, al is 0 before and after it, and exactly one completion pulse is generated.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, choose a nonzero clk_cnt, issue WRITE with din=1, and model the bus as released-high except drive external SDA low during the WRITE stable-high phase when scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1.
elements.expected_response: At the arbitration-loss response edge, al asserts, the command is aborted without cmd_ack, idle asserts, and both scl_oen and sda_oen are high, releasing SCL and SDA. This is the holding side of the requirement's port behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model to identify the WRITE stable-high arbitration check and response edge; sample al, idle, scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack after each posedge and assert al=1, idle=1, scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, and cmd_ack=0 at that edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, issue WRITE with din=0, and during the stable-high phase keep external SDA low as required by the driven data bit; allow SCL to rise normally and do not inject an unexpected STOP.
elements.expected_response: No arbitration loss is detected: al remains low and the active WRITE sequence does not return to idle or apply the arbitration-loss release response. During the active write-high phase, sda_oen remains low to drive SDA low, while SCL follows the normal WRITE phase; therefore the ports do not show the arbitration-loss side of the requirement (both enables high with idle asserted).
elements.check_method: At the modeled WRITE stable-high phase, compare al, idle, scl_oen, and sda_oen against the normal WRITE reference model; assert al=0, idle=0, sda_oen=0, and that the outputs are not the simultaneous arbitration-loss response scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 with idle=1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=1000 (READ) while idle. Allow the READ sequence to release sda_oen and release SCL for the read window. Drive the external SDA line so the filtered SDA signal is stably 0, then cause a filtered SCL rising edge before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: at the filtered SCL rising edge during the active READ data-sampling phase, dout becomes 0, equal to the filtered SDA value.
elements.check_method: At each filtered_scl_rising event while read_sequence is active and before cmd_ack, sample ssda and compare it with dout after the corresponding posedge update. Require dout == ssda and record separate coverage for ssda=0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=1000 (READ) while idle. Reach the READ data-sampling phase with sda_oen released, drive the bus so ssda is 1, and cause a filtered SCL rising edge before cmd_ack. Enable a fault-injection or mutation mode that prevents dout from capturing the filtered SDA value at this edge, such as retaining its previous 0 value.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting, non-holding side of shows: dout is different from the filtered SDA value at the filtered SCL rising edge, and the requirement checker reports a REQ-0133 violation; the DUT must not be accepted for this behavior.
elements.check_method: At filtered_scl_rising during read_sequence, compare dout after the posedge with ssda. With ssda=1 and the injected dout=0 behavior, require the checker to flag dout != ssda and classify the result as a failed requirement check.

elements.stimulus: With ena high, issue a READ command, have the external device drive SDA low, and provide a valid SCL high transition that propagates through synchronization and filtering as a filtered SCL rising edge while filtered SDA is low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the clock edge at which filtered SCL rises, dout updates to 0, the filtered SDA value.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for synchronization, filtering, and filtered-edge detection; sample dout after the posedge and compare it with ssda on the same detected filtered_scl_rising event.

elements.stimulus: With ena high, issue a READ command, have the external device drive SDA high, and provide a valid SCL high transition that propagates through synchronization and filtering as a filtered SCL rising edge while filtered SDA is high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the clock edge at which filtered SCL rises, dout updates to 1, the filtered SDA value.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for synchronization, filtering, and filtered-edge detection; sample dout after the posedge and compare it with ssda on the same detected filtered_scl_rising event.

elements.stimulus: With ena high, issue a READ command and establish a filtered SCL low level with dout=0. Then change the external SDA level so that filtered SDA becomes high while keeping SCL low, and hold SCL low long enough to observe multiple enabled clock edges without a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: dout does not update to the filtered SDA value because no filtered SCL rising edge occurred; dout remains 0 despite ssda becoming high.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm filtered_scl_rising is absent during the SDA transition, then assert that dout remains equal to its pre-transition value on every subsequent sampled clock edge.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous reset, then release nReset. Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue cmd=READ (1000) while idle. During the READ data-bit sampling phase, release SDA and drive the external bus so filtered SDA is stably high before and at a filtered SCL rising edge; keep al=0 and resets inactive.
elements.expected_response: Shows side: when filtered_scl_rising=1 during read_sequence, dout updates to 1, the sampled filtered SDA bit supplied as the received READ data bit, and remains available through command completion.
elements.check_method: At each filtered_scl_rising probe event within read_sequence, sample dout after the posedge nonblocking updates and compare it with ssda; require dout==ssda for the sampled bit and record a bin for sampled value 1.

elements.stimulus: Complete a READ sampling event that sets dout=1, then issue another cmd=READ with ena=1 and no reset or arbitration loss. During the next READ data-bit sampling phase, release SDA and drive the external bus so filtered SDA is stably low before and at filtered SCL rising. Observe dout immediately after that edge.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise side: if dout remains 1 or otherwise fails to update to the new filtered SDA value 0 at the READ filtered SCL rising edge, the port exhibits the non-requirement behavior and the checker must report a REQ-0135 violation; dout must not retain the stale value.
