elements.check_method: At filtered_scl_rising within read_sequence, compare post-edge dout against ssda and against the pre-edge dout value; flag failure when ssda=0 but dout is not 0, particularly when it incorrectly retains the prior value 1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=0001 (START), and clk_cnt=16'h0004. Hold cmd at START and provide clock edges through the interval before the first clk_en tick, as determined by the divider reference model.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the required difference: idle remains asserted throughout every clock before clk_en; the FSM does not enter the START sequence, and no command-completion pulse is produced during this pre-tick interval.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking updates settle, compare the idle probe and command-sequence probes against the divider/reference-model clk_en prediction; require idle=1 while clk_en=0.

elements.stimulus: Continue the same transaction with ena=1 and cmd=0001 (START) until the reference-model divider asserts clk_en, while keeping the bus released high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting, advancing side of the required difference: on the enabled clk_en opportunity, the FSM leaves idle and enters the START command sequence; idle deasserts and the START output phase begins.
elements.check_method: Detect the modeled clk_en tick and, after the corresponding registered update, compare idle and start_sequence probes. Require idle to transition from 1 to 0 and start_sequence to assert only after that permitted advancement.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, deassert it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then apply cmd=4'b0001 (START) and hold it through the next enabled clk_en edge while the bus is released high.
elements.expected_response: The idle decoder selects START: scl_oen enters the START command-specific sequence, initially releasing SCL and subsequently driving SCL low after the SDA-low-while-SCL-high phase, rather than remaining in idle behavior.
elements.check_method: At posedges after reset and after the enabled acceptance edge, compare the scl_oen waveform with the reference model for the START sequence and confirm that the observed sequence is not the idle released-line hold.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, deassert it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then apply cmd=4'b0010 (STOP) and hold it through the next enabled clk_en edge while the bus is released high.
elements.expected_response: The idle decoder selects STOP: scl_oen enters the STOP command-specific sequence, releasing SCL high during the STOP generation instead of remaining in idle behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare sampled scl_oen values and their phase ordering after the enabled acceptance edge against the STOP reference-model sequence, including the transition to the released-SCL phase.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, deassert it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then apply cmd=4'b1000 (READ) and hold it through the next enabled clk_en edge with external SCL and SDA initially high.
elements.expected_response: The idle decoder selects READ: scl_oen enters the READ command-specific sequence, including the released-SCL read window and subsequent SCL-low phase, rather than remaining in idle behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model to compare the scl_oen waveform from the enabled acceptance edge through the READ sequence and verify the expected release-to-low phase ordering.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, deassert it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then apply cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE), drive din=0, and hold the command through the next enabled clk_en edge with external SCL high.
elements.expected_response: The idle decoder selects WRITE: scl_oen enters the WRITE command-specific sequence, releasing SCL for the write high phase and then driving SCL low, rather than remaining in idle behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed scl_oen phase sequence after the enabled acceptance edge against the WRITE reference model and confirm that it differs from the idle released-line hold.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, deassert it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then apply cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) and hold it across multiple enabled clk_en edges while the bus is released high.
elements.expected_response: The idle decoder selects no operation: scl_oen remains in the idle released-line behavior and no command-specific output-enable sequence begins.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen for the entire observation window and compare it with the idle reference waveform; flag any command-sequence transition as a failure.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller into idle, set ena=1 and cmd=4'b0001 (START), provide a released-high I2C bus, and continue clocking through the next clk_en tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed difference: the recognized START command moves the FSM out of idle into start_sequence; idle deasserts and start_sequence asserts.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered updates, compare idle, start_sequence, and the other command-sequence probes against a command-decoding reference model; require start_sequence=1 and idle=0 after command acceptance.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller into idle, set ena=1 and cmd=4'b0010 (STOP), and continue clocking through the next clk_en tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed difference: the recognized STOP command moves the FSM out of idle into stop_sequence; idle deasserts and stop_sequence asserts.
elements.check_method: Sample the FSM probes after each posedge and compare them with the reference command decoder; require stop_sequence=1 and idle=0 after acceptance.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller into idle, set ena=1 and cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE), drive din to either 0 or 1, and continue clocking through the next clk_en tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed difference: the recognized WRITE command moves the FSM out of idle into write_sequence; idle deasserts and write_sequence asserts.
elements.check_method: Compare idle and write_sequence probes after the enabled timing tick with the reference FSM model; require write_sequence=1 and idle=0 for both din values.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller into idle, set ena=1 and cmd=4'b1000 (READ), and continue clocking through the next clk_en tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed difference: the recognized READ command moves the FSM out of idle into read_sequence; idle deasserts and read_sequence asserts.
elements.check_method: Compare idle and read_sequence probes after the enabled timing tick with the reference FSM model; require read_sequence=1 and idle=0.

elements.stimulus: For each cmd value in {4'b0000, 4'b0011, 4'b0101, 4'b0110, 4'b0111, 4'b1001, 4'b1010, 4'b1011, 4'b1100, 4'b1101, 4'b1110, 4'b1111}, reset or otherwise return the controller to idle, set ena=1, drive that cmd value, and continue clocking through multiple clk_en ticks.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of the observed difference: NOP (0000) and every unsupported command leave the FSM in idle; idle remains asserted and start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence remain deasserted, with no command sequence entered.
elements.check_method: For every listed command, compare all five FSM probes after each enabled tick against the reference model; require idle=1 continuously and all four command-sequence probes=0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 to model a released-high bus. Set ena=1 and issue cmd=4'b0001 (START), holding the command until it is accepted; observe scl_oen and sda_oen through the START command-generation window.
elements.expected_response: The port follows the holding side of observed_via: scl_oen remains 1 throughout the released-line and SDA-low START phases; sda_oen is initially 1 with scl_oen=1, then transitions to 0 while scl_oen remains 1. No interval may pull SDA low before or while SCL is driven low.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, use a temporal assertion that the START sequence contains scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 before a later phase with scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=0, and assert scl_oen never becomes 0 from command acceptance through the SDA-low phase. Record bins for released-line phase, SDA-low phase, and ordered 1-to-0 sda_oen transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, keep ena=1 and drive cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) for at least the duration of a START command window, then repeat with an unsupported command encoding such as cmd=4'b0011; observe scl_oen and sda_oen.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting, non-holding case is checked: because no START command is issued, the START-specific sda_oen 1-to-0 transition while scl_oen remains 1 must not occur, and scl_oen must not be driven low by a START sequence. The otherwise side of observed_via is therefore absent: scl_oen does not become 0 before or during an SDA-low START phase, and sda_oen does not show the START transition.
elements.check_method: Use temporal assertions from each command presentation until it is removed that scl_oen remains 1 and sda_oen remains 1, with no START-sequence state or output transition. Compare against the positive START trace to ensure the 1-to-0 sda_oen transition is conditional on cmd=START.

elements.stimulus: Deassert both resets, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=START, and wait for the filtered START condition to be generated. Continue clocking through the terminal START-sequence phase without asserting reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed behavior: after the START condition, scl_oen becomes 0 for the final phase, the FSM enters idle, and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock cycle at command completion. cmd_ack is low on the following clock.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, use a scoreboard keyed to the detected START sequence. Check scl_oen=0 before the completion acknowledgement, idle=1 with cmd_ack=1 at the completion edge, and cmd_ack=0 on the next edge; assert that no additional acknowledgement occurs without a new command.

elements.stimulus: Deassert both resets, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=START, and wait until the filtered START condition is generated and the START sequence is active. Assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the terminal completion edge, then release nReset and clock the DUT.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise case of the observed behavior: reset aborts the START completion, so scl_oen is not driven low as the completion effect, cmd_ack remains low rather than pulsing, and the FSM is reset to idle.
elements.check_method: Monitor outputs immediately after the asynchronous reset assertion and on subsequent settled clock edges. Check scl_oen=1, idle=1, and cmd_ack=0, and verify that no delayed cmd_ack pulse or completion-phase scl_oen=0 occurs after reset release unless a new START command is issued.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold the bus released and present cmd=0010 (STOP) with ena=1 until the command is accepted; keep rst=0 and nReset=1 and allow the sequence to run through cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the STOP sequence, sda_oen becomes 0 first, showing SDA is driven low; only afterward scl_oen becomes 1, showing SCL is released high. The ordered phases occur before cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, record the first cycle with sda_oen=0 and the first subsequent cycle with scl_oen=1. Assert that the SDA-drive cycle precedes the SCL-release cycle and that cmd_ack occurs after both observations; cover the ordered transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, present cmd=0010 (STOP) with ena=1 while SDA is initially released, and monitor sda_oen and scl_oen on every settled posedge from STOP acceptance until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the otherwise behavior must never occur—scl_oen must not become 1 before sda_oen has become 0. Any observation of scl_oen=1 while sda_oen has not previously been 0 is a failure because it releases SCL in the wrong order.
elements.check_method: Use a temporal assertion that, from STOP acceptance until cmd_ack, a rising transition or value of scl_oen=1 is permitted only after a prior sampled sda_oen=0. Flag and cover any premature SCL release as the forbidden side of the observed_via 'otherwise' condition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1 and cmd=STOP (4'b0010) while the external bus is released high. Allow the STOP sequence to ensure SDA is low, release SCL, and wait until sscl becomes high; sample before cmd_ack asserts.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of shows: after SCL is high, sda_oen is high, releasing SDA while SCL remains high to generate the STOP condition. The STOP command subsequently completes with exactly one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a bus model and cycle-accurate monitor to detect the STOP phase through stop_sequence, scl_oen=1, and sscl=1. Assert sda_oen=1 on every cycle from that phase until cmd_ack, and verify the SDA line is high and cmd_ack is a one-cycle pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1 and cmd=STOP (4'b0010), but hold the shared SCL line externally low after the controller releases SCL. Keep the external SCL low for multiple clk_en opportunities while observing the STOP sequence.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting otherwise side of shows: while SCL has not become high, sda_oen remains low, so SDA is not released prematurely during the STOP sequence. The controller waits for filtered SCL high; after the external hold is removed and sscl becomes high, it must then release SDA with sda_oen=1 before completing the STOP command.
elements.check_method: Monitor stop_sequence, scl_oen, sscl, slave_wait, sda_oen, and cmd_ack. While scl_oen=1 and sscl=0, assert sda_oen=0 and no cmd_ack; then release the external SCL low drive and assert that sda_oen transitions high only after sscl=1 and before the single completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1, cmd=0010 (STOP), clk_cnt=0, and model the bus as released high. Run clock cycles until the STOP sequence drives SDA low, releases SCL high, then releases SDA high.
elements.expected_response: When the STOP sequence has released SCL high and SDA high, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock; scl_oen and sda_oen are both 1. This is the holding side of the observed port behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, monitor the idle probe, cmd_ack, scl_oen, and sda_oen. Assert that idle is high and cmd_ack is high on the completion edge, cmd_ack is low on the immediately following clock, and both output enables are 1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1, cmd=0010 (STOP), clk_cnt=0, and externally hold SCL low when the STOP sequence releases SCL; keep SDA available for the controller. Do not allow filtered SCL to become high, so the STOP sequence cannot release SDA high and complete.
elements.expected_response: Because the STOP sequence has not released SCL high and SDA high, the requirement's completion condition does not hold: cmd_ack remains low and the FSM does not return to idle while clock stretching persists. This is the otherwise side of the observed port behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor filtered SCL, the stop_sequence and idle probes, scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack on every settled posedge. While filtered SCL remains low after SCL release, assert that stop_sequence remains active or waiting, idle remains low, and no cmd_ack pulse occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=READ (4'b1000), and provide a released-high bus. On the enabled clock, issue the READ command and keep the external SDA participant able to drive either value until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the READ data-bit window after command acceptance and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 1. This is the holding side of shows: SDA is released so the external slave can drive the data bit.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge from entry into read_sequence through the READ data-bit window until cmd_ack, assert sda_oen==1; correlate the interval with the read_sequence probe and verify no cycle in that interval drives SDA.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=0, cmd=WRITE (4'b0100), and provide a released-high bus. On the enabled clock, issue the WRITE command and observe its data-bit phase.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit phase, sda_oen is 0 for din=0. This is the contrasting otherwise side of shows: SDA is driven low rather than released for an external slave.
elements.check_method: At the settled posedge identifying write_sequence's data phase, assert sda_oen==0 and compare it against din=0; ensure the observed driven-low interval is distinct from the READ data-bit window.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) while idle, and continue driving the released-high bus through the READ data-bit phase until the controller completes the bit.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of observed_via.shows: after the READ sequence begins, scl_oen becomes 1 during the READ data-bit window, releasing SCL, and subsequently becomes 0 to pull SCL low before command completion.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked waveform assertion/reference FSM keyed to read_sequence: record the first READ data-bit phase with sda_oen=1, require scl_oen=1 throughout the released-SCL window, then require a later scl_oen=0 transition before the READ command's cmd_ack pulse; sample registered outputs after each posedge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100) while idle with din=0, and observe the active bit-transfer phase through completion.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise case of observed_via.shows: because the controller is not executing a READ data-bit phase, scl_oen must follow the WRITE sequence rather than show the READ-specific released-high read window followed by its READ-phase low transition; no READ sequence is entered.
elements.check_method: Check the idle/read_sequence/write_sequence probes and correlate them with scl_oen. Assert that read_sequence remains deasserted and compare scl_oen only against the WRITE phase reference waveform, ensuring no interval is falsely classified as the REQ-0145 READ window.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena high and issue a READ command with clk_cnt=0. Drive the external bus so the filtered SCL signal produces successive rising edges, with filtered SDA stable at 0 for one rising edge and stable at 1 for a later rising edge.
elements.expected_response: For the holding case in observed_via.shows, on each rising edge of filtered SCL, dout is updated on the corresponding registered clock update to the actual filtered SDA value represented by ssda: first 0, then 1.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for synchronization, filtering, and filtered-SCL edge detection. At each detected filtered_scl_rising event, sample dout after the posedge nonblocking updates and compare it with ssda for that event; require both data values to be captured.

elements.stimulus: Continue the READ sequence after establishing dout=0 on a filtered SCL rising edge. Change the external SDA input so that the filtered SDA value becomes 1 while keeping filtered SCL low and preventing any subsequent filtered SCL rising edge for several enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: For the otherwise case in observed_via.shows, dout is not updated to the current filtered SDA value when filtered SCL does not rise; dout remains at its previously captured value of 0 throughout the interval.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm ssda changes to 1 while filtered_scl_rising remains deasserted. Sample dout after each enabled posedge and require it to retain 0 until a new filtered SCL rising edge occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high I2C bus, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000), and allow the complete READ bit cycle to execute, including the filtered SCL rising edge that captures the slave-driven SDA value and the terminal low phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after the READ bit cycle completes, the FSM reaches idle and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock; cmd_ack is low on the surrounding clocks. dout contains the filtered SDA value captured at the filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for READ phase progression and filtered SCL timing. At the modeled terminal completion, compare the idle probe and verify a one-clock cmd_ack pulse with no additional pulse before the next command.

elements.stimulus: After accepting cmd=READ with ena=1 and entering the READ sequence, assert rst=1 on a clock edge before the filtered SCL rising edge or terminal low phase completes; deassert rst and continue clocking without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the aborted READ does not complete, so cmd_ack does not assert at the would-be READ completion; reset returns the FSM to idle and clears cmd_ack. No delayed acknowledgement is emitted after reset.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack on every clock from reset assertion through the modeled original READ completion window and verify it remains low, while checking that the idle probe is asserted after synchronous reset and that no post-reset pulse occurs without a new accepted command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and issue cmd=WRITE with din=0 while the bus is released and no arbitration loss or reset occurs; drive the bus normally through the WRITE data phase until cmd_ack asserts.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data phase while the controller sets the transmitted data bit, sda_oen is 0, meaning SDA is driven low. This is the din=0 side of the required sda_oen mapping.
elements.check_method: Use a transaction monitor triggered by the WRITE data-phase probe or equivalent phase timing; sample registered sda_oen after each posedge and assert sda_oen==0 whenever din==0 in that phase, with no mismatch before the single cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and issue cmd=WRITE with din=1 while the bus is released and no arbitration loss or reset occurs; drive SDA high externally or leave it undriven, and run the transaction through the WRITE data phase until cmd_ack asserts.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data phase while the controller sets the transmitted data bit, sda_oen is 1, meaning SDA is released high. This is the din=1 side of the required sda_oen mapping.
elements.check_method: Use a transaction monitor triggered by the WRITE data-phase probe or equivalent phase timing; sample registered sda_oen after each posedge and assert sda_oen==1 whenever din==1 in that phase, with no mismatch before the single cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, apply cmd=0100 (WRITE) while idle with din=0, and hold din=0 through the WRITE data-output phase until completion or abort.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-output phase, before cmd_ack and absent reset or arbitration loss, sda_oen is 0. This is the din=0 side of the requirement: SDA is driven low through the active-low output-enable control.
elements.check_method: Monitor the write_sequence probe and sample sda_oen after each posedge clk; assert that whenever write_sequence is active in the data-output phase, sda_oen=0 while din=0, and record no violation before cmd_ack or abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, apply cmd=0100 (WRITE) while idle with din=1, and hold din=1 through the WRITE data-output phase until completion or abort.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-output phase, before cmd_ack and absent reset or arbitration loss, sda_oen is 1. This is the din=1 side of the requirement: SDA is released high through the active-low output-enable control.
elements.check_method: Monitor the write_sequence probe and sample sda_oen after each posedge clk; assert that whenever write_sequence is active in the data-output phase, sda_oen=1 while din=1, and record no violation before cmd_ack or abort.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, then deassert reset with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=WRITE (0100), din=1, and external SDA and SCL released high. Wait for command acceptance from idle and allow the WRITE sequence to run to completion without external arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the WRITE stable-high phase, sda_chk is asserted and scl_oen is 1, releasing SCL. In the following completion phase scl_oen becomes 0, the FSM returns to idle, and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock. This is the required side of the observed port behavior.
elements.check_method: Use cycle-aligned assertions and a reference model to identify WRITE acceptance and completion. Assert that sda_chk overlaps the stable-high WRITE phase, that scl_oen has the ordered values 1 then 0 before cmd_ack, that idle is asserted at completion, and that cmd_ack is high for one clock only.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, then deassert reset with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=WRITE (0100), din=1, and external SCL released high. After the WRITE phase releases SCL and enables arbitration checking, force external SDA low for the stable-high arbitration sample to cause arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: al asserts, the WRITE command aborts, and the FSM returns idle with both output enables released. cmd_ack does not pulse, and scl_oen does not complete the required released-high then driven-low sequence before a WRITE completion pulse. This is the otherwise side of the observed port behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor sda_chk and the filtered SDA sample to confirm the injected arbitration loss occurs during the stable-high phase. Assert al and idle, assert no cmd_ack for the aborted command, and compare the scl_oen/cmd_ack trace against the positive completion sequence to ensure no normal completion sequence is produced.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=START, clk_cnt to a small nonzero value, and provide a released-high bus; hold the command inputs stable until the START sequence is accepted and completes.
elements.expected_response: During the complete START sequence, scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0. The output-enable behavior is the shows side of REQ-0151: scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 in released phases, scl_oen=0 when SCL is actively pulled low, and sda_oen=0 when SDA is actively pulled low while SCL is high. No output enable value is interpreted as a high drive.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge from sequence entry through cmd_ack, compare scl_o and sda_o against 0 and check the expected phase-by-phase scl_oen/sda_oen values against a START-sequence reference model; assert that any enabled line is externally observable only as low or released-high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a WRITE command with ena=1 and din=0 on a released-high bus. Allow the command to progress through the SDA drive phase, released SCL high phase, and final SCL-low phase until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting release-versus-drive case follows the shows side of REQ-0151: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0 throughout; sda_oen=0 during the WRITE data-low drive phase and sda_oen=1 during the released SDA phase, while scl_oen=1 during the released SCL high phase and scl_oen=0 when SCL is pulled low. If the enables were not active-low or the constant-low outputs were replaced by high drive values, this would be the otherwise side and the check must fail.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_o, sda_o, scl_oen, and sda_oen after each registered update through completion, correlate each value with the WRITE phase reference model, and additionally pull the external SDA line high during the release phase and low during the drive phase to confirm that the DUT does not source a high level.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and both external SCL and SDA lines initially high. Observe the START phase in which SDA is pulled low while SCL remains released.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed behavior: scl_o=0 and sda_o=0 remain constant; scl_oen=1 indicates SCL is released, while sda_oen=0 indicates SDA is actively pulled low.
elements.check_method: At every clock after registered outputs settle, compare scl_o and sda_o against 0 and compare scl_oen/sda_oen against the expected START-phase values using a waveform scoreboard.

elements.stimulus: Complete a START command to establish busy, then issue a STOP command with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and the external SCL line high. Observe the final STOP phase after SCL is released, when SDA is released while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting release case of the observed behavior: scl_o=0 and sda_o=0 remain constant; scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 indicate that both SCL and SDA are released rather than actively pulled low.
elements.check_method: At the final STOP phase, sample the registered output enables after the posedge and verify both are 1 while the constant-drive outputs remain 0; also verify the corresponding bus lines resolve high when the external driver is released.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the external SCL line released high, and issue a WRITE command (cmd=0100) with din=0. Observe the WRITE sequence through its released-SCL high phase and the subsequent phase where the controller pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: During the following SCL-low phase, scl_oen is 0 and scl_o is 0; this is the holding case showing that the SCL line is driven low through the active-low SCL output enable.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, correlate the registered scl_oen and scl_o values with the reference FSM phase and open-drain bus model; require scl_oen==0 and scl_o==0 during the SCL-low phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the external SCL line released high, and issue a WRITE command (cmd=0100) with din=0. Sample the stable high phase before the controller advances to the following SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: During the stable high phase, scl_oen is 1 while scl_o remains 0. This is the contrasting case: scl_o being low is not evidence that SCL is driven low because the SCL output enable is released.
elements.check_method: At the settled posedge for the WRITE stable-high phase, compare scl_oen and scl_o against the reference model; require scl_oen==1, scl_o==0, and the modeled bus SCL remains high absent an external low driver.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the external SDA line released high, and issue a WRITE command (cmd=0100) with din=0. Observe the data-drive phase in which the controller presents the write zero before releasing SCL.
elements.expected_response: During the write-zero data phase, sda_oen is 0 and sda_o is 0; this is the holding case showing that the SDA line is driven low through the active-low SDA output enable.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge in the WRITE data phase, correlate sda_oen and sda_o with din and the reference FSM; require sda_oen==0 and sda_o==0, and verify the open-drain bus model resolves SDA low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the external SDA line released high, and issue a WRITE command (cmd=0100) with din=1. Observe the data-drive phase before the controller releases SCL.
elements.expected_response: During the write-one data phase, sda_oen is 1 while sda_o remains 0. This is the contrasting case: sda_o being low is not evidence that SDA is driven low because the SDA output enable is released.
elements.check_method: At the settled posedge for the WRITE data phase, compare sda_oen and sda_o against the reference model; require sda_oen==1, sda_o==0, and the modeled bus SDA remains high absent an external low driver.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=START, and model both external pull-ups with no external low drive. Issue the START command and observe the initial released-bus phase before the controller pulls SDA low.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in REQ-0154: scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, so both SCL and SDA are released and the resolved SCL and SDA lines are high due to the external pull-ups.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare scl_oen and sda_oen with the open-drain bus-resolution model. Require scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==1 and, with no external low drive, require resolved_scl==1 and resolved_sda==1 during the released phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=START, and model both external pull-ups with no external low drive. Issue the START command and continue through the phase where SDA is pulled low while SCL remains released, followed by the phase where SCL is pulled low.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case in REQ-0154's observation: when sda_oen=0, SDA is actively pulled low rather than released, and when scl_oen=0, SCL is actively pulled low rather than released. The corresponding resolved line is low despite the external pull-up.
elements.check_method: At settled posedges in the SDA-low phase require sda_oen==0 and resolved_sda==0 while scl_oen==1 and resolved_scl==1. In the subsequent SCL-low phase require scl_oen==0 and resolved_scl==0. Verify the observed output-enable polarity and resolved open-drain line values against the bus-resolution model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=START while the bus is released high; provide normal released-high SCL/SDA conditions and allow the START sequence to reach its terminal phase without reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at START sequence completion, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle, then deasserts on the immediately following clk cycle.
elements.check_method: Use a scoreboard keyed to the observed START terminal phase; sample cmd_ack after each posedge and require the pattern 1,0 at terminal and next cycle, with no additional assertion before the next command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=STOP from a busy transaction; provide normal bus conditions so the STOP sequence reaches completion without reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at STOP sequence completion, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle, then deasserts on the immediately following clk cycle.
elements.check_method: Detect the STOP terminal phase from the reference model and compare registered cmd_ack on that posedge and the next posedge, requiring one asserted sample followed by one deasserted sample.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ; release SDA and provide a stable external SDA value while allowing SCL to rise and the READ sequence to complete without stretching, reset, or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at READ sequence completion after the low phase, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle, then deasserts on the immediately following clk cycle.
elements.check_method: Use the READ reference model to identify its terminal phase, then assert that cmd_ack is high on exactly that completion cycle and low on the next cycle and all subsequent idle cycles.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive din=0, and issue cmd=WRITE; provide normal bus responses and allow the WRITE sequence to complete without arbitration loss, reset, or clock stretching.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at WRITE sequence completion, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle, then deasserts on the immediately following clk cycle.
elements.check_method: Track the WRITE terminal phase with a timing-aware reference model and compare cmd_ack at terminal and terminal-plus-one clk, requiring a single-cycle pulse only.

elements.stimulus: Repeat a normal START command with ena=1 and a released-high bus, then monitor cmd_ack at the modeled START completion and for at least two following clk cycles.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: cmd_ack must not remain asserted for more than one clk cycle; any high value on completion must be followed by cmd_ack=0 on the next clk.
elements.check_method: Add an assertion that forbids consecutive cmd_ack=1 samples across the START terminal boundary and flags a two-or-more-cycle pulse.

elements.stimulus: Repeat a normal STOP command with ena=1 and normal bus conditions, then monitor cmd_ack at the modeled STOP completion and for at least two following clk cycles.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: cmd_ack must not remain asserted for more than one clk cycle; the STOP completion observation is invalid if cmd_ack is high on both completion and the next clk.
elements.check_method: Check the terminal-cycle pulse width with a consecutive-cycle assertion and record failure if cmd_ack remains high beyond the required one-cycle interval.

elements.stimulus: Repeat a normal READ command with a valid external data bit and no reset, arbitration loss, or stretching, then monitor cmd_ack at and after the modeled READ completion.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: cmd_ack must not be absent at READ completion and must not be asserted for multiple consecutive clk cycles; either condition violates the required pulse behavior.
elements.check_method: At the reference-model terminal event, require cmd_ack=1 for the completion sample and cmd_ack=0 for the next sample; classify missing or extended pulses separately.

elements.stimulus: Repeat a normal WRITE command with din=1, provide SDA high during the released high phase to avoid arbitration loss, and monitor cmd_ack at and after the modeled WRITE completion.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: cmd_ack must not be absent at WRITE completion and must not remain high on the following clk; either missing or extended behavior is nonconforming.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed cmd_ack sequence against the expected terminal pattern 1,0 using the timing-aware WRITE reference model.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt, present cmd=START while the filtered bus is released high, and allow the START sequence to reach its terminal SDA-low/SCL-low phase without reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: after the terminal START output-enable phase, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle, then deasserts on the next clock; no additional acknowledge pulse occurs, and a subsequent bit command may be presented after completion.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked assertion comparing cmd_ack with the reference-model terminal phase: require cmd_ack==1 on exactly the first registered cycle after terminal-phase completion and cmd_ack==0 on the following cycle and all other cycles; correlate the pulse with the observed scl_oen/sda_oen terminal phase.

elements.stimulus: First establish a busy transaction state, then set ena=1 and present cmd=STOP with the bus available; allow the STOP sequence to reach its terminal SDA-release-while-SCL-high phase without reset.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: when the terminal STOP output-enable phase is reached, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle and returns low on the next clock, permitting the next bit command to be issued.
elements.check_method: Monitor the registered output enables and reference-model terminal phase, then assert that cmd_ack is a single-cycle pulse aligned with STOP completion and is not high in either adjacent completion cycle.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and present cmd=READ; release SDA for the external slave, drive a valid returned data bit, allow any required SCL stretching to end, and let the READ sequence reach its terminal SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: after READ reaches its terminal output-enable phase and captures the bit, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle and is low thereafter until another command completes.
elements.check_method: Use the reference timing model to identify READ terminal completion despite variable prescaling and stretching; compare the sampled cmd_ack waveform against a one-cycle pulse at that completion and check no early, late, or multi-cycle assertion.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, drive din=0, and present cmd=WRITE; provide a normal released-high SCL response with SDA matching the driven write bit, and allow the WRITE sequence to reach its terminal SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: once the terminal WRITE output-enable phase is reached, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle, then deasserts with no repeated pulse.
elements.check_method: Correlate write_sequence and the final scl_oen/sda_oen phase with cmd_ack using a cycle-accurate scoreboard; require one and only one high cmd_ack sample at completion and low samples before and after it.

elements.stimulus: While idle with ena=1, drive cmd=NOP (0000), then drive unsupported encodings such as 0011 and 1111 for multiple enabled timing ticks without issuing START, STOP, READ, or WRITE.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise side of shows: no command reaches a terminal START, STOP, READ, or WRITE phase, so cmd_ack remains deasserted; it must not assert spuriously or remain asserted for any cycle.
elements.check_method: Check idle remains asserted and no command-sequence terminal phase occurs; use an assertion that cmd_ack==0 for the entire NOP/unsupported-command interval, including consecutive enabled clk_en ticks.
